500238|2026-06.headline: Whirlpool of India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.4% to INR 2,582 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% on war-led oil/forex costs and e-waste accounting.
500238|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 11.4% to a record INR 2,582 crore, with management citing record Faridabad output, completed sell-in/sell-out of the new-regulation refrigerator and AC range, and gains in premium categories. Profitability was squeezed: EBITDA was about INR 120 crore at 4.6%, down roughly 377 bps, as oil-linked inputs, a roughly 10% rupee depreciation to 95-96 per dollar, Haryana minimum wage revisions and an e-waste accounting charge were only partly recovered through price. Consolidated revenue rose 12.1% to about INR 2,727 crore with EBITDA at 5.1%. Management guided that July-September will be the weakest quarter and gave no full-year numbers.

financial_highlights.change: +11.4% YoY, highest ever for a quarter

financial_highlights.value: FY25 up 4%, FY26 up 7%, Q1 FY27 up 11%
financial_highlights.change: from declines in Q1 and Q2 FY26
AC receivables collected; 5 of last 8 quarters negative

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Management said AC is about two-thirds of revenue and was the weakest margin category under the new regulations; Q1 AC sales were up about 50% in the company's outlet KPI and AC shipments rose in April-May ahead of the summer.

segments.name: Refrigerators
segments.commentary: Launched the 654-litre Luxuriem side-by-side with triple evaporator and Intelli Crisper, priced against INR 70,000-80,000 competitor side-by-sides; company previously had no presence above 500-600 litres, and Pune plant began shipping in July.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Washer sales grew over 80% in the quarter per management; Dynamix dispenser now on 50% of the range, and 11 kg top-load launched in Juniper Green. Top-load segment described as highly competitive.

segments.name: Kitchen appliances (Elica)
segments.commentary: Elica revenue and profit growth were cited as strong; management said there is no remaining minority stake to buy and the holding sits with Pralhad Bhutada.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management said predicting it is 'close to zero' accuracy.
July-September 2026 expected to be the weakest quarter, with margins lower than April-June but not as low as the year-ago period.
Management aims for above 10-20% AC growth over the next two years, pacing growth to avoid channel stock build-up.
Management expects war-related and e-waste headwinds to ease if resolved, with an equitable e-waste solution sought from government.
Company aims for 10% share of top-load washers in time; 12-15 months of new product launches planned.
capex_capacity: Pune plant started production in July 2026, shipping Luxuriem refrigerators, with INR 245 crore invested in the facility (as stated).
Faridabad plant delivered record manufacturing output in Q1 FY27 despite war and heat-wave supply constraints.
Current utilisation of about 70-75% on an annual basis; management said no immediate capex need in the next 6-12 months.
Capex is an ongoing process; management said cash is not a constraint and capital goes to projects with strong ROI.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in April and May 2026 only partly offset war-led and regulatory cost increases, creating a net under-recovery.
Management said the company led hikes only in April and May and avoids unilateral moves that could cost share, citing 2022 experience.
Competition in top-load washers has intensified; the company lost share in that segment while gaining elsewhere.
Distribution is near 10% share in some regions versus about 3% in smaller ones; not present at Croma, Vijay Sales or Reliance Digital (per analyst question).

qa_highlights.question: Parent refinancing and plans for the remaining stake; the cash on the balance sheet.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent, Whirlpool Corporation, holds 39.75% and it does not discuss parent matters. The board is examining capital use across manufacturing expansion, automation and inorganic opportunities, with no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue growth and margin expectations, including whether OPM could be flat year on year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide; it said the outcome depends on war, forex and regulatory developments, and that margin protection is a focus.

qa_highlights.question: Whether industry can pass on further price hikes, and the elasticity of a 10% increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price coordination is illegal and that it decides pricing independently; a 5% price move equals about INR 1,000 per unit, and not all cost inflation will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the about 400 bps margin compression between war, regulation and P4G actions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war impact (oil and forex) was larger than the regulatory impact; P4G savings were largely offset as input-supply constraints limited negotiation leverage, and fixed costs were held flat as a percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Sale of services to the parent (INR 250 crore in FY25) and ESOP vesting terms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transitional services agreement runs to 2029 on a cost-plus, arm's-length basis; ESOPs were issued at market value with performance-linked vesting and a 3-year cliff.

risks_watch: Oil-linked input costs (MDI, polyol, EPS, plastics) and rupee at about 95-96 per dollar; about 30% of raw materials imported and several Middle East-sourced items are single-sourced.
E-waste accounting provision: management is seeking an equitable industry solution and said the impact is significant.
July-September weakness in AC, which is about two-thirds of revenue.
Price competition in top-load washers and whether the company can hold share while raising prices.
Parent Whirlpool Corporation at 39.75% stake and undisclosed capital-allocation plans.
500238|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and new launches, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly declined to quantify full-year outcomes and attributed the margin squeeze to war, forex and regulation. Evasive on the parent's capital plans and the remaining stake.
key_quotes: Revenue is up 26% and profits are up 22%.

rows.why: Management is seeking a government-backed equitable e-waste solution and calls the impact significant; a resolution would ease margin pressure but none is confirmed.

rows.why: Net working capital turned negative in June 2026, with 5 of the last 8 quarters negative, as AC receivables were collected.

500241|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn, but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 13.7% amid SPP UK service-mix shift and Rs 389 mn labour-code charge.
500241|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn with EBITDA of Rs 2.093 bn (14.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.121 bn. Full-year revenue was flat-to-marginally up at Rs 45.380 bn (+1%), with EBITDA of Rs 6.213 bn (13.7%) and PAT of Rs 3.772 bn. Domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 while Q4 grew 3%; international grew 7% for the year and 25% in Q4. Management attributed the year's shortfall to JJM funding delays, a foundry ERP transition, and a Rs 389 mn labour-code charge classified as exceptional. Order books grew strongly: domestic Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%).

segments.name: Domestic (standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 28.281 bn (-3%); Q4 Rs 9.091 bn (+3%). Order growth led by building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water; JJM is about 4-5% of revenue but hit water-sector shipments.

segments.name: International - SPP UK
segments.commentary: EBITDA fell from Rs 95 crore to Rs 58.1 crore (Rs 37 crore drop), driven by a shift from high-margin services to products as UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit.

segments.name: International - SPP US
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 300 crore in FY22; about 35% from fire pumps and 25% from data centres. EBITDA down about Rs 3 crore per management.

segments.name: International - other entities
segments.commentary: Dutch, South African and other entities grew; South Africa margin % lower but absolute EBITDA higher. Management said Q4 was a slower first quarter for some entities due to prior-year spillover timing.

guidance_outlook: Management will strive for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 in both domestic and international businesses, but cited war and gas-supply risks.
SPP UK margins expected to realign toward the target level by roughly the calendar Q3 2026, with full-year margins targeted back to desired levels.
Labour-code impact of Rs 389 mn in FY26 (Rs 258 mn in Q4) treated as exceptional; estimates may be revised as rules are notified.
Final dividend of Rs 7 per Rs 2 share (350%) recommended, subject to AGM approval.
Management expects JJM-related disruption to ease over the next few quarters; AMP8 inquiries are expected to convert from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Foundry ERP (SAP) transition at Kirloskarvadi caused temporary disruption; management says the system has largely stabilised.
Company has five foundries; the largest was the focus this year, and in-house electricity capacity was added to hedge gas shortages.
Eight US data-centre packages were on the shop floor at the US plant as of the call.
Nuclear: full-scale primary heat transport pump prototype is to be delivered to NPCIL on schedule; budgetary quotes given for all pump types; Bharat SMR (200 MW) quotes sought.
demand_pricing: Standalone order inflow growth came from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power (coal and nuclear), and water and irrigation.
Company says it earns premiums against multinationals on lifecycle cost and efficiency, and enforces advance payment or LC for small and medium pumps; retail sold on cash.
Management says it can pass on raw-material price rises; Hormuz-related disruption raised costs.

SPP US competes with Amstel, Taco, Grundfos and Xylem in data-centre cooling; management says it is not cheaper but offers plug-and-play containerised packages with 18-24 month data-centre lead times.
US distributors rose to about 46 from 12 four years ago; roughly 10 states have no coverage.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the strong standalone orders coming from, and what else is disrupting execution beyond JJM?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water. Execution was hit by the foundry ERP transition and JJM fund-release delays at the state level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international margins fall despite strong order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said the SPP UK mix shifted away from services because UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit. Margins are expected to realign by about calendar Q3 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Would FY26 have grown at double digits without the disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said Q4 sales exceeded last year's Q4 and growth should resume, but war and gas uncertainty remain. He declined to give a precise FY27 figure beyond striving for double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear opportunity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has indigenously designed primary-side pumps, with budgetary quotes given. Orders are expected step by step as NPCIL and DAE constraints clear; SMR prototype orders are expected once the design is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: How diversified is the US business, and what is the 3-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Fire is about 35% of US business and data centres about 25%; the rest is municipal and booster packages. Focus is HVAC, municipal markets and AMP8-style programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall across international entities in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said Q4 is seasonally slower for some entities due to prior-year spillover, and that year-on-year all entities except SPP UK improved.

risks_watch: SPP UK service mix and margin recovery timing (calendar Q3 2026 target).
JJM second-phase tendering and state-level fund release; no meaningful tendering pickup yet.
Geopolitical shocks (Middle East war, gas and fertiliser supply), with management citing cost pressure.
Foundry ERP stabilisation and dispatch conversion of the Rs 24.7 bn domestic order book.
Data-centre demand, where management acknowledged a mild US delay; ECA financing is a dependency.
Further labour-code revisions could change the Rs 389 mn exceptional charge.
500241|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on order book, nuclear and data-centre opportunities, but cautious and evasive on FY27 growth, citing wars and gas shortages. Management was candid that FY26 margins and volumes were hit by SPP UK mix and operational transitions. Several questions on order-book breakdown and aftersales share were declined.
key_quotes: the double-digit growth that we expected was actually impacted by the first quarter, second quarter and third quarter.
So we do expect that we will get back to that level.
We're not cheaper, but we changed the model before to a modular model, and we provide a container system to them.

rows.why: SPP UK EBITDA fell from Rs 95 crore to Rs 58.1 crore (Rs 37 crore drop) on mix shift away from services, and management expects margins to realign toward target by about calendar Q3 2026; FY26 EBITDA margin was 13.7% versus Q4's 14.8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line quantified; eight US data-centre packages are on the shop floor as an order-driven build and a SMR/nuclear prototype is due to NPCIL on schedule, but no capacity addition has a date attached.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic order book Rs 24.680 bn (+30% YoY) and international order book Rs 14.808 bn (+21% YoY) back management's aim to strive for double-digit FY27 revenue growth, though war and gas risks were flagged and FY26 revenue grew only 1% to Rs 45.380 bn.

rows.why: Capex was not discussed directly; utilisation was not disclosed, so an announcement hinges on order conversion and the nuclear and data-centre pipeline rather than a stated capacity gap.

rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance only as an aspiration to 'strive' for double-digit growth and declined to give a precise figure, citing war and gas-supply risks.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution was hit in FY26 by JJM fund-release delays (about 4-5% of revenue), the foundry ERP transition and SPP UK idling; domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 and Hormuz-related cost pressure persists.

rows.why: Nuclear primary heat transport pump prototype is due to NPCIL on schedule and Bharat SMR (200 MW) quotes are sought, but orders are expected step by step as NPCIL and DAE constraints clear, with no launch date.

rows.label: Domestic and international order book build
rows.why: Domestic order book Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%) give a large backlog to dispatch, though foundry ERP stabilisation and JJM delays gate conversion.

rows.label: AMP8 inquiries converting to orders
rows.why: Management said AMP8 inquiries are expected to convert from the next quarter and JJM disruption should ease over the next few quarters, but there is no meaningful tendering pickup in JJM yet.

rows.label: Labour-code charge revision
rows.why: The Rs 389 mn FY26 exceptional charge (Rs 258 mn in Q4) may be revised as labour-code rules are notified, which could move reported profit though not the operating run-rate.

tone.note: Management was confident on order book, nuclear and data-centre pipeline and SPP UK margin recovery by calendar Q3 2026, but cautious and evasive on FY27 growth citing war and gas risks; analysts pressed on FY26 shortfall and order-book breakdown, which management declined to fully detail.

500241|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.
500241|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to Rs.1,306 million, a margin of 11.8%. Standalone domestic revenue grew 9% to Rs.6,738 million, EBITDA 16% to Rs.920 million, and PAT 15% to Rs.540 million. International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

financial_highlights.change: driven by SPP USA and Kirloskar Brothers Thailand
moderated due to lower services contribution

segments.name: Standalone domestic (KBL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.6,738 million (+9%), EBITDA Rs.920 million (+16%), PAT Rs.540 million (+15%). Domestic pending order book Rs.25,577 million excluding small pump order book.

segments.name: International (overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, led by SPP USA and KBT Thailand. EBITDA Rs.207 million at 5.1% margin. Overseas pending order book Rs.15,045 million.

segments.name: SPP USA
segments.commentary: Growing 20-plus% in the quarter, driven by data centers, fire and HVAC projects; a multi-year framework with a large US data center operator is near signing (under NDA).

segments.name: SPP UK / Rodelta (Netherlands)
segments.commentary: SPP UK margin pressure from lower services revenue as chemical/petrochemical service contracts idled; management expects services recovery from Q2 FY27 for SPP UK and Q3 for KBL. Rodelta losses widened on delayed execution; improvement expected over the next two quarters.

segments.name: KPML (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Margin fell from 12.5% to 7.3% after merger of loss-making TKSL (steel castings) into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable.

Services business expected to recover from Q2 FY27 at SPP UK and from Q3 at KBL, lifting blended overseas margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventories and advances rising and is dispatch being withheld, hindering double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory built up during the foundry upgrade, which is now complete; some orders were half-finished, so full shipments slipped. Improvement was seen in the current month and is expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: When will the services expansion lift SPP UK margins, and what is the outlook for Rodelta?
qa_highlights.answer: SPP UK services expected to restart in Q2 FY27 (Q3 for KBL) as power plant and water utility contracts ramp. Rodelta delays are due to consolidating Dutch entities; improvement expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated margin down from 13% in Q4 to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone EBITDA margin was 13.7% vs 12.8% last year; the drop was mainly SPP UK. Management agreed margins should recover as services revive from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the domestic order book executes in FY27, and what drove the power order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of the ~Rs.2,500 crore domestic order book expected in FY27. Power growth is largely nuclear, with primary and secondary circuit orders received in Q1 and new thermal plants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the KPML margin fall from 12.5% to 7.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to the merger of loss-making TKSL into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable on BHEL and KBL demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is normally equal to depreciation, used for modernisation, debottlenecking and quality. No specific figure was given.

500241|2026-09.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to Rs12,767 million, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.3% and order intake jumped 68%.
500241|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 24% YoY to Rs12,767 million and EBITDA grew 16% to Rs1,432 million at an 11.2% margin, while consolidated order intake rose 68% YoY to Rs20,472 million. Standalone domestic revenue grew 23% to Rs7,991 million with PAT up 45% to Rs544 million, but standalone gross margin compressed about 400 bps, which management attributed to commodity cost inflation. The international (SPP UK, SPP USA, Dutch group) business grew 24% in revenue but EBITDA margin was only 5.3%, as UK service revenue lagged and oil and gas, a lower-margin segment, ramped up. Management guided to margin recovery in H2 and to double-digit standalone revenue growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: margin moderated; no YoY figure stated

segments.name: Standalone domestic
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs7,991 million (+23% YoY), EBITDA Rs937 million (+37%), PAT Rs544 million (+45%). Domestic order book Rs29,264 million as of September 2026, +29% YoY, excluding small pumps order book.

segments.name: International (SPP UK, SPP USA, Dutch group)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by SPP UK, SPP USA and Dutch group. EBITDA Rs233 million at 5.3% margin, dragged by lower services contribution. Overseas pending order book Rs17,013 million, +32%.

segments.name: Small pumps (retail)
segments.commentary: Grew 12% per press release; management said roughly 50% of that came from price and the balance from volume. Small pumps order book excluded from the Rs29,264 million domestic order book.

segments.name: Power / nuclear
segments.commentary: Power order book rose from about Rs600 million to Rs700 million sequentially per analyst. Nuclear orders for canned motor pumps and primary-side safety package were valued at roughly Rs60-70 crore combined per management.

segments.name: Oil and gas (UK/US)
segments.commentary: Oil and gas order intake picked up in UK and US (Louisiana projects, CP2, Plaquemine, Qatar NFPS, Guyana), with lower margins and higher employee costs; management said this is a drag on UK margins.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to improve in H2 FY27; international H2 expected to be noticeably better than H1 per Alok Kirloskar.
Double-digit standalone revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 remains the target.
UK margins: absolute levels similar to CY24 / FY25 levels expected next year, but oil and gas mix may keep margins from recovering fully until the following year.
Standalone gross margin compression attributed to commodity price rise (copper, gun metal, steel); expected to normalise over next few quarters.
Services share of SPP UK business is about 35%; target about 40% at KBI BV level over a 3-year cycle.
capex_capacity: Large consignments are pending dispatch, causing higher inventory; management expects these to go out in subsequent months, reducing inventory and lifting margins.
Working capital rose roughly Rs225 crore standalone and about Rs250 crore consolidated in H1, per analyst; management attributed it to WIP for long-lead capital goods (8-12 month lead times).

Nuclear: 32 primary coolant pumps tender for three plants (NPCIL/Tarapur); bids reportedly open 21 January 2027, first technical bid then financial bid. Casting qualification passed; a foundry was found.
demand_pricing: Standalone price increase of about 10% taken since January, per analyst; management says the company is a price leader and passes through commodity costs to a large extent.
Competitors facing supply issues (foundry closures, LPG shortage, wage code changes), which management says is enhancing market share.
Thermal, nuclear, oil and gas, fertilizer and power are driving capital goods orders; data centres in India are just starting.
UK domestic industrial demand is weak per management (electricity at Rs30/unit); growth is from oil and gas exports, data centres and fire pumps for warehousing; AMP8 not yet material.
Fire pump market worldwide about $0.5 billion, increasingly commoditised by Chinese FM/UL-certified entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Will international margins recover in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Margins expected to rise in H2, with the UK's fourth quarter (Jan-Mar) seeing more service contracts kick off; UK service business was down in the first two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much of UK margin recovery is expected and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said FY26 UK margins were about 7%; FY27 will recover but not to FY25 levels. Material cost up 8% in UK, and oil and gas mix lowers margins; next year similar margins to CY24 in absolute terms, with percentage recovery likely later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of small pump growth between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Rama Kirloskar said about 50% of the 12% growth came from value (price) and the balance from volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear order value and tender status?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said canned motor pump and primary-side safety package orders together are about Rs60-70 crore. Tender for 32 primary coolant pumps issued; company says material qualification is now proven.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin compress and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed compression to commodity price rises, not legacy contracts or mix; said it will normalise over coming quarters and there is no material gap between small pumps and engineered pumps.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a 15% margin aspiration in 1-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar declined to give a figure, saying competition for nuclear and power orders will be strong and pricing depends on operations and material costs.

risks_watch: International EBITDA margin at 5.3% with UK services lagging; margin recovery depends on services contracts kicking off in Q3/Q4 FY27.
Standalone gross margin compression of about 400 bps tied to commodity inflation; pass-through may moderate.

Order intake is lumpy; management said orders are recognised only once commercial terms are agreed.

500245|2026-03.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q4 FY26 PBT rose to INR514 crore from INR432 crore, with FY27 casting volume target of about 1.85 lakh tonnes.
500245|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 pig iron production fell 3% YoY to 1,58,152 tonnes after a roughly 3.5-month Hiriyur blast furnace stoppage cut FY26 output by about 68,000 tonnes. Casting volumes grew 13% in Q4 and 7% for the year, helped by Oliver Engineering in Rajpura, while tube production rose 6% in Q4. Management said pig iron prices recovered in Q4 and into April, with reported PBT of INR514 crore versus INR432 crore a year earlier. Management guided to 15% volume growth in FY27 and an EBITDA margin of about 12.5%, below its 15% comfort level.

financial_highlights.change: approx. INR 100 crore improvement on PBT per management

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Q4 production 1,58,152 t (down 3% YoY); Q4 sales 1,27,600 t (down about 6% from 1,35,000 t). FY26 production 6,23,939 t vs 6,31,103 t; Hiriyur stoppage cost about 68,000 t.

segments.name: Castings (incl. Oliver)
segments.commentary: Q4 production 36,596 t (up 13%) and sales 34,980 t (up 9%). FY26 production 1,48,564 t (up about 7%); including Oliver, about 1.62 lakh t, with Oliver contributing about 23,000 t (16% of sales).

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Q4 production 56,119 t (up 6%) and sales 51,106 t (flat vs 51,500 t). FY26 production 2,16,914 t vs 1,99,443 t; FY26 sales 1,88,700 t vs 1,68,800 t.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Q4 production 58,119 t (down about 10%) and sales 24,812 t (up 20% from 20,700 t). FY26 production about 2.40 lakh t vs 2.42 lakh t, hit by two fume-extraction shutdowns.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 118-119 crore on about 17,000 t; FY27 target about 24,000-25,000 t and INR 240-250 crore. Monthly run rate was 1,700 t in Jan-Mar and about 1,800 t in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 casting volume target about 1,85,000 t (management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t, production basis), with 2-3% foundry rejection causing a small gap to sales.
FY27 overall sales volume growth of at least 15%, conditional on commodity prices not falling again.
Tube volume growth of 10-11% targeted in FY27 via debottlenecking; management expects about half of the 10% realisation drop (5-6%) to be recovered.
EBITDA margin expected to be just above 12.5%; management comfortable only at 15%.
Solar and wind power: about 35 MW solar and 25 MW wind to be commissioned June-September 2026; FY27 benefit about INR 45 crore, rising to about INR 90 crore at full run-rate.
Capex of about INR 600-700 crore per year, including about INR 500 crore for a bigger-diameter tube mill at Baramati (completion in about 1.5 years).
Oliver merger into KFIL targeted within a couple of months, to count for FY26.
capex_capacity: Solapur foundry running at about 4,200 t/month against a 6,000 t/month minimum expectation (about 70% utilisation); target about 5,000 t/month and 55,000-56,000 t sales in FY27.
Oliver Rajpura run rate about 1,700 t/month in Jan-Mar; target 2,000 t/month average and 24,000-25,000 t in FY27.
Sixth large-casting foundry being commissioned; seventh foundry planning started. Long-term feasibility up to 3 lakh t/year castings.
Baramati seamless tube capacity to rise from 2.30 lakh t to 4 lakh t by adding 1.5 lakh t; 1.5-year project for bigger tube mill.
Hiriyur blast furnace upgrade for about INR 125-150 crore to 2.5-3 lakh t/year; Koppal oxygen plant of 150 t/day by year end, with oxygen enrichment to 5% from 2.5% and PCI to 160-170 kg from 130 kg.
Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines, beneficiation and pellet plant planned; 52 MW waste-heat power in operation; Jejuri at about 30% green power.
demand_pricing: Pig iron prices up INR 5,000/t vs October and INR 4,000/t vs December (per management); international pig iron at about $475/t. Q4 realisation lagged due to order-book lag and some spill into January, with further price correction in April.
Casting realisation about INR 125/kg in base; management expects it to go beyond INR 130/kg within two years, with INR 10-12/kg of commodity-linked reductions expected to partly flow back.
Three new casting customers added in Q4 (diesel engine maker, tractor and earthmoving exporters); export share rose from 20% to 28% and CV share from 12% to 16% (per analyst's figures).
Oliver machining value expected to reach about INR 100 crore within a year, with 22 HMCs installed.
Cost pressures: rupee at about INR 95/$ and coal up about $25/t, which management expects to be partly passed on.
Tube NSR about INR 1,13,000/t at FY26 end; management expects tube prices to rise in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 casting target of 1.85-1.9 lakh t still achievable given slower ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t as target, with about 1.05 lakh t from Koppal, 60,000 t from Solapur and 25,000 t from Oliver; the 45,000 t/quarter run rate expected within a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory and backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects just above 12.5% EBITDA, aims for 15% and cited coke self-sufficiency, 52 MW waste-heat power, Jambunath mines and pellet plant as backward integration steps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 pig iron price hikes lag and how will Q1 FY27 spreads move?
qa_highlights.answer: Lag came from 15-day order books and monthly commitments to regular customers; price increase effect partly in April. Management said pig iron price increase is inevitable but coal and coke costs are rising, and it is still assessing spreads.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost saving from solar, wind and captive power?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar delivered about INR 70 crore benefit in FY26; wind and solar commissioning June-September should add about INR 45 crore in FY27, with INR 90 crore possible at full run-rate after new Maharashtra regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Tube business order book and ONGC orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the pending order figure; expects new tenders this year and better domestic and export oil and gas demand. Targets 10-11% volume growth in tubes.

qa_highlights.question: Tube capacity expansion and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bigger tube mill at Baramati about INR 500 crore, within a 1.5-year completion; total capex about INR 600-700 crore per year, with borrowings reduced.

Oil and gas tube orders (including ONGC) remain unconfirmed; management had no current order book figure.

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal (Unique PMS): what drove the ~INR100 crore YoY and ~INR50 crore QoQ jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR58 crore of the increase is power and fuel, split roughly INR28-29 crore rate-driven and INR28 crore volume-driven, with Rajpura castings volumes and a full-month Jejuri run versus last year's shutdown. Power trading (about INR10 crore a year) has stopped and green power use is now limited to 8 hours instead of 17.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: does the regulation change hit the solar and wind savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, and payback stretches from 3 years to 3.6-3.7 years. Battery storage at MW scale is being examined, with some power expected through batteries shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: what is the INR350 crore contingent liability for forest development fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka levied forest development fees in 2016; the company won in the High Court, the state appealed to the Supreme Court, and the matter is sub judice after hearings with orders reserved. The company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Mody (individual investor): will the company move into subassemblies, machined components and high-end castings, and what is the status of 3D printing?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine shops at Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura already supply fully machined components, including a 6-cylinder head to an OEM. Maximum casting size after expansion is about 3 tons, the 2-part foundry is about 1,250 t per month, and the company is not yet in mining or wear-resistant parts. Prototyping is near serial production, with 50 cylinder blocks bought via the proto route.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): what is Q1 EBITDA margin and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q1 company EBITDA at 12-13%, with steel and tube margins at 14-17% and pig iron weighing on the blend. Castings target about 15% plus or minus 1%, with pricing upside, and tubes are in a wait-and-watch phase due to Chinese dumping. Management expects company margin to improve on pig iron support and pass-through from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: what are current pig iron realisations and how much did raw-material costs absorb?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation moved from a base of about INR39,000/t to about INR42,400/t QoQ. Management said dollar rates and coal costs are pressuring costs, but realisation still improved slightly net of cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruvesh Kanakia (Antique): what volumes are expected for the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Pig iron close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less. Castings gross sales to rise from about 162,000 t to about 188,000 t (17-20% growth). Steel external sales of 100,000-110,000 t vs about 84,000 t, and tube volumes up at least 10%, with overall volume growth of at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Manish Goyal (Thinkwise): timeline for INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration, seventh foundry, and ONGC/OIL tube order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Castings realisable capacity of 270,000 t is targeted in this year plus two years, with 300,000 t in 3-4 years; tubes to 350,000 t in 3-4 years after the expander mill (2 years to build); steel external sales of 240,000 t in about 2 years. Blast furnace 1 conversion to steelmaking is expected to be decided within 2-3 months, with commissioning in about 2 years. The 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch): will coking coal costs rise further next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company holds about 3 months of coal stock, so the high-cost coal flows through June-August, which will be higher than April-June. Peaks may be partly mitigated as coal prices ease and blending improves.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi: is pig iron realisation a blend of foundry and steel grade, and what is capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly pig iron sales plan is about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external), a mix of grades with foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t. Capex is INR600-700 crore this year, rising in later years, with about INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years. Green power capex is set to slow, with battery storage starting at 50-70 MW.

qa_highlights.question: Anurag Patil (Quest): what is the net impact on annual power cost after solar, wind and power trading changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 70 MW solar to yield INR70-80 crore a year, the 35 MW solar about INR30 crore, and the windmills (equivalent to 55 MW) to add more, with the combined solar and wind benefit at about INR70-80 crore. Seasonal wind benefit is about 70% in June-September. Koppal is self-sufficient on waste-heat power, but Maharashtra fuel costs need a strategy and power trading is not likely to return without battery storage.

risks_watch: Power and fuel cost inflation: about INR58 crore of YoY increase, LPG in Solapur roughly doubled, and coking coal peaking June-August; watch whether castings and alloy steel price pass-through actually lands in Q2-Q3.

Tube volume recovery: tube sales down 14% YoY with a weaker mix; Chinese dumping and subdued oil and gas and export demand; the INR100 crore-ish order book from ONGC/OIL is expected to finish within two quarters.

Green power economics: regulatory limit cut from 17 to 8 hours, power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped, and solar and wind savings cut to about INR80 crore from about INR100 crore; payback moved to 3.6-3.7 years.

Execution of capex: INR600-700 crore this year against INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years; Solapur 2-part foundry by October 2026, solar and wind commissioning June-September 2026, Koppal oxygen and PCI by February-March 2027.
Pig iron pricing and exports: realisation up to about INR42,400/t from INR39,000/t; about 30,000 t exported; a dollar and coal cost squeeze could offset gains.
Contingent liability of about INR350 crore on Karnataka forest development fee, sub judice at the Supreme Court with no timeline.

I think we are on this direction though still the aggregates could be a little far away.
So I would say that I'm optimistic and we should look for improved performance in the coming quarters.
We can't push too much of line pipes into market.
There is a negative impact, but we continue to progress because still there is benefit.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has given new volume guidance (castings 17-20%, pig iron near 700,000 t) and expects pricing gains from Q2-Q3, but tube demand is weak with Chinese dumping and Q1 tube sales down 14% YoY, so an upgrade depends on tube recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY, green-power savings cut from about INR100 crore to about INR80 crore a year, coking coal peaks June-August, and tube volumes fell 14% YoY; pig iron may come in slightly below 700,000 t.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Premium couplings plant in Baramati with an order expected within weeks, and 6-cylinder head supplied to an OEM; no firm product launch date given.

rows.label: ONGC/OIL tube order (about INR100 crore, 23,000 t) execution
rows.why: Management said the 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters, supporting tube volume recovery against Q1 tube sales down 14% YoY.

rows.label: Green power rule change and end of power trading
rows.why: Green power use cut from 17 to 8 hours and power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped; solar and wind savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, payback stretches to 3.6-3.7 years.

rows.label: Karnataka forest development fee contingent liability (about INR350 crore)
rows.why: Matter is sub judice at the Supreme Court with orders reserved; company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability, so an adverse ruling is a risk with no set timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on pig iron pricing, castings demand and capacity additions, but cautious and wait-and-watch on tubes given Chinese dumping; analysts probed the other-expenses jump, green-power savings, Q1 margin trajectory, and the pass-through on alloy steel, which management left vague.

500245|2026-09.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 2,057 crore, while PBT of Rs 138 crore was held back by tube margin pressure and casting rejections.
500245|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 topline was Rs 2,057 crore versus Rs 1,755 crore a year earlier (+16%), with PBT of Rs 138 crore against Rs 120 crore. Casting sales of Rs 633 crore (+30%) and pig iron of Rs 581 crore (+20%) led growth, while tubes grew only 0.5%. Realisations rose across pig iron (+12.4%), castings (+6.8%), steel (+7.6%) and tubes (+1.6%), though management said margins remain under pressure in castings and tubes. Management flagged a casting rejection problem at Solapur and an expected tractor-segment slowdown.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 120 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.metric: H1 pig iron hot metal production

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 581 crore (+20% YoY); external pig iron volume about 1,34,000 t vs 1,28,000 t (+3.5%). One export cargo of 31,000 t was shipped at better realisation than domestic. Realisation Rs 43,054/t (+12.4%).

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 633 crore (+30%); gross casting sales crossed 50,000 t for the first time, net sales 47,888 t (+20%). Realisation Rs 1,30,000/t (+6.8%). Solapur about 15,000 t/quarter; Rajpura about 6,000 t+ in a quarter.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: External steel sales Rs 206 crore (+48% YoY); realisation Rs 77,500/t (+7.6%). Steel production H1 up about 14%.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales growth only 0.5% in value; volume 48,547 t (about -2%). Realisation +1.6%. Management said margins are under pressure, with Q1 volumes weak on delayed oil and gas projects.

guidance_outlook: Tube volumes targeted above 1,00,000 t in H2 FY27 to show growth over last year.
Casting net sales targeted to stabilise at about 1 lakh t in each of the next two quarters; management said casting capacity and rejections are being addressed to reach this level.
Solapur utilisation to rise to 6,000 t/month (18,000 t/quarter) across both foundries, with a 70,000 t/annum target for Solapur.
Pig iron domestic volume expected to be better than last year, at about 6.6-6.7 lakh t; oxygen enrichment and PCI at Koppal blast furnaces 1 and 2 due by year-end.
Medium-term target of 15% volume growth per year in castings; long-term pig iron sales target of 0.5 million t.
Machining value to cross Rs 100 crore annually within a year or two, with about 60% expected as contribution.
capex_capacity: Solapur second foundry line (two-part/no-bake, large castings up to 2 t): phase one and two nearly complete; commissioning expected by January 2027; total foundry capacity 15,000 t/annum (1,250 t/month).
Rajpura phase two targeted by March 2027 to take capacity to about 4,000 t/month; phase three needed for 70,000 t/annum; Rajpura stabilised at about 2,200 t/month with rejections falling.
Koppal alloy steel plant: technology partners engaged; equipment ordering and commercial negotiation under way; about 20 months execution after a 2-3 month start.
Jejuri rolling mill expansion, Baramati expander mill and Ahmednagar small piercing mills: execution stage; timelines not specified.
Machining capex about Rs 200 crore to date (per management correction from Rs 240 crore); annual machining value about Rs 50-60 crore (about Rs 5 crore/month).
Only 35 MW of wind power commissioned at Solapur; other windmills not yet commissioned.
Hiriyur mini-blast furnace upgrade planned; all three mini-blast furnaces together could give 8.5-9 lakh t of pig iron output before conversion to steel.
demand_pricing: Casting demand strong from automotive, earth-moving and stationary engine segments; foundries fully loaded in Q2 and October. Management flagged possible small corrections in tractor demand.
Casting contracts use a quarter-on-quarter price pass-through, so some further price increases are still to be realised.
Pig iron is priced on a monthly spot basis; coking coal is the main cost driver, while iron ore costs have been broadly stable.
Tube demand held back by delayed oil and gas projects; Chinese dumping expected to ease after anti-dumping duty was extended for five years; US exports hit by the war situation.
Pig iron exports were uneconomic for internal plants at current prices, per management; export opportunities will be taken only occasionally.
Rejections at Solapur about 10-11%, expected to fall to 7-8% next quarter; Rajpura rejections expected below 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Solapur phase two demand visible, and where is the Jejuri steel project and the Koppal alloy steel plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Solapur phase one and two are nearly complete and ramping up (about 15,000 t/quarter). Koppal alloy steel ordering is under way, with about 20 months of execution after a 2-3 month start. Jejuri and other projects have seen delays but are in execution.

qa_highlights.question: Why did casting margins contract despite higher volume and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quarterly price pass-through lags, unfinished windmill commissioning, and productivity and quality work still needed. Further price realisation is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Was pig iron export a conscious choice, and what is the domestic run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export cargo was a short window of better prices that also eased domestic pressure. Volume is expected to be about 6.6-6.7 lakh t, rising as Koppal oxygen enrichment and PCI are added.

qa_highlights.question: How much casting volume will the large-casting line add in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects no meaningful volume in FY27, with meaningful volume in FY28 as some parts move from makeshift arrangements to formal production.

qa_highlights.question: Why are tube volumes flat and margins down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was weak because oil and gas projects were delayed, and Q2 margins were still under pressure from low-priced orders. Realisation improvement is expected from new orders, with one large export consignment slipping into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is machining revenue low relative to investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machining capex is about Rs 200 crore and revenue is about Rs 50-60 crore a year; the gap reflects customer model changes and infrastructure. Target is Rs 100 crore within a year or two, with customer co-investment and special-purpose machines.

qa_highlights.question: Is casting capacity sufficient for customer demand, and what is the rejection trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer commitments exceed 3 lakh t per annum, so new capacity or acquisitions are being evaluated. Solapur rejections are expected to fall to 7-8% from 10-11% next quarter.

risks_watch: Casting gross-to-net gap: rejections of about 3-4% and Solapur thin-wall rejections at 10-11% need to fall as guided.
Tube margins and volumes: H2 target of over 1 lakh t depends on oil and gas project execution, with Chinese imports and weak US exports as headwinds.
Tractor segment demand softening, which management flagged as a possible risk to casting volumes.
Machining utilisation: customer model changes have led to 50-60% of capacity being bought, against the Rs 100 crore target.
Management succession: leadership transition is in progress with no timelines disclosed.
Project execution timelines: Koppal alloy steel (about 20 months from order), Jejuri rolling mill and Rajpura phase two (by March 2027) may slip.
500245|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth, pricing and casting demand, but cautious on tube margins, casting rejections and project timelines. Management repeatedly qualified targets with 'hopeful' and 'quite optimistic' language and avoided committing to pig iron price direction.
key_quotes: So, it looks like we have come out of the low commodity cycle, gradually going up.
I am quite hopeful, confident that this change will come and we will see further improvement in the tube.
Total foundry capacity would be 15,000 metric tons per annum.
And we will continue to focus and continue to grow on the casting volumes in coming years because we have lined up new customer additions as well as the existing customers.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew 16% YoY to Rs 2,057 crore and casting demand is strong, but management was qualified ('hopeful', 'quite optimistic') and tube and tractor risks remain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tube volumes were down about 2% YoY in Q2, tube demand depends on delayed oil and gas projects, management flagged a possible tractor-demand softening, and the Solapur line already slipped to January 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Koppal alloy steel plant needs about 20 months of execution after a 2-3 month start, so output is beyond the window; the Solapur large-casting line (up to 2 t) gives no meaningful FY27 volume and only moves to meaningful volume in FY28.

rows.label: Solapur large-casting line (up to 2 t) ramp
rows.why: Management expects no meaningful volume in FY27 and meaningful volume in FY28 as parts move from makeshift arrangements to formal production.

rows.label: Casting quarter-on-quarter price pass-through
rows.why: Casting realisation rose 6.8% YoY to Rs 1,30,000/t and management said further price increases are still to be realised under quarterly pass-through contracts.

rows.label: Machining value to Rs 100 crore
rows.why: Machining value is about Rs 50-60 crore a year against about Rs 200 crore of capex, and 50-60% of capacity is currently bought, so the Rs 100 crore target depends on customer co-investment and new models.

500249|2026-06.headline: KSB H1 FY27 revenue INR 12,920 mn with weak Q1 sales (2–3% growth); management targets double-digit FY growth on H2 export recovery.
500249|2026-06.overview: Management presented at an institutional investor meet (held 19 Aug 2026) covering H1 FY27 (April–June 2026 quarter as described in the call). H1 revenue from sales was INR 12,920 mn, EBITDA INR 1,465 mn and PBT INR 1,279 mn. Management attributed the subdued quarter to Middle East export shipments held up by the geopolitical situation, supply-chain constraints on castings after gas availability issues, a delayed KUSUM 2.0 solar scheme, and slow project-pump order inflow. Management expects a much better H2 and aims for double-digit growth, though it flagged NPCIL test-bed delays on nuclear and continued fixed-price margin pressure.

financial_highlights.change: Management said Q1 sales grew only 2–3% over the prior period
Well below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay
Down from mid-teens levels the analyst cited; management called it temporary

segments.name: Order intake mix
segments.commentary: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves about 19% of order intake, per management.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order on hand INR 1,235 crore covering GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5 and 6 and the Kudankulam safety package; Shirwal nuclear capacity at 80–90% utilisation with a new shed adding about 7,000 sq m (about 20% plant capacity).

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Margin fell to single digits in H1 on commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales; management expects a return to double-digit margins.

segments.name: SupremeServ
segments.commentary: Management targets 25–30% aftermarket share in India (group target 35%); business growing about 15% per annum.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar pumps are 5–7% of current order book versus a 10–12% target; Maharashtra tender orders expected to help in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Goal is double-digit growth for the full year; management said 15–17% average growth over time is achievable (10–15% volume, about 15% value).
H2 expected to be much better, with export shipments recovering from Middle East disruption and supply chain now around 85–90% stable.
Nuclear GHAVP testing expected to start in September 2026 once NPCIL resolves test-bed issues; first pump needs about 500 hours of testing (2–3 months), with up to six pumps a year possible.
EBITDA target of 13–14% reiterated; gross margin under pressure on fixed-price project business, partly offset by internal cost reduction.
Export order book about 15% of sales, with a target of 20%.
S/4HANA implementation in H1 of next year, with group cost allocation expected in FY28 OpEx; amount not yet decided.
Capex of about INR 80–120 crore per year (sustenance plus growth).
capex_capacity: Shirwal plant is about 115,000 sq m (15,000 sq m added with recently bought land); a new shed of about 7,000 sq m adds about 20% capacity.
Shirwal capacity about 1,200–1,300 pumps across energy, oil and gas and nuclear combined.
Nuclear: first indigenous pump made in 2025, under testing at NPCIL test bed in 2026; ISO-19443 certified.
Reciprocating pumps being developed under BP&CL technology; EIL approval in process, requiring a running pump supplied within 12 months.
Split-case pump of 10,000 cubic metres per hour under development for export and river-linking projects.
demand_pricing: Management sees energy (thermal, nuclear, renewable) and water/wastewater infrastructure as main growth drivers; supercritical thermal boiler circulation pump win broke an import jinx.
Project market (oil and gas, petrochemical) slowed; Dangote refinery expected to contribute later.
Price increases: foundry costs up 12–15%; KSB standard market price hikes so far single-digit, being phased in.
Export demand hit by Middle East war and earlier US tariffs cancelling some orders; US boiler feed pump orders for gas plants noted.
Data centre: orders from KSB Germany's OEM customers and an international OEM in India for liquid cooling; no size quantified.
Pump content of projects estimated at 3–5% of total project value.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 performance subdued, and how much export was to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the war affecting exports (pumps ready but undelivered) and supply-chain constraints; sales grew only 2–3%, and H2 is expected to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is double-digit growth; nuclear test-bed delay is the main risk, which management sees as low risk. 20% top-line is possible but with peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution and competition for the next primary coolant pump tender?
qa_highlights.answer: GHAVP testing delayed by NPCIL test-bed issues, with testing expected from September; a new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) expected in a few months, and KSB is the approved supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
500249|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.
key_quotes: So, we are looking for a good outlook, not short-term, but long-term.

But we expect a much better half in the second half, because as of today, we see that the issues related to supply chain, of course, have not been fully solved, but it is much better that we have now a bit of consistency in the supply chain after having agreed with them on the revised prices.
Our goal is to have a double -digit growth. This is what we are aiming for.
So I see these as temporary variations.
So whatever you see investment of INR 80 crores, INR 100 crores, INR 120 crores annually, we intend to do that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterates 13-14% EBITDA margin and good double-digit valves margin, but valves fell to single digits in H1 and fixed-price project margins remain under pressure with foundry costs up 12-15% and pass-through lag of 3-6 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shirwal nuclear capacity is at 80-90% utilisation and a new 7,000 sq m shed adds about 20% plant capacity, under construction, though no commissioning date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 10-15% volume growth for FY27 but Q1 sales grew only 2-3% and H2 recovery rests on Middle East export shipments and supply stabilisation at 85-90%, with no quantified timeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at INR 80-120 crore a year, with Shirwal nuclear utilisation at 80-90%, but no new plant or board-level capex plan was announced on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 sales growth was 2-3% against a double-digit full-year goal, and management has offered few hard numbers on H2 recovery, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 growth of 2-3% against a 10-15% volume goal, the NPCIL test-bed delay pushing GHAVP testing to September, and the KUSUM 2.0 delay (solar H1 revenue INR 50-60 crore) all put the double-digit target at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Reciprocating pumps under BP&CL technology await EIL approval needing a running pump within 12 months, and a 10,000 cu m/hr split-case pump is under development, but no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Nuclear primary coolant pump tender (about eight reactors)
rows.why: A new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) is expected in a few months and KSB is the approved supplier, against an order on hand of INR 1,235 crore.

rows.label: Order book growth from H1 order intake
rows.why: H1 FY27 order intake was INR 15,307 mn (excl. Nuclear) and the order book reached INR 27,445 mn in June 2026, with management citing a 14% intake CAGR.

rows.label: Standard market price hikes being phased in
rows.why: Foundry costs are up 12-15% and KSB standard price hikes so far are single-digit and being phased in, with a 3-6 month pass-through lag.

tone.note: Management was confident on nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities and on the double-digit full-year goal, but defensive on the 2-3% Q1 sales growth and vague on H2 timing; analysts pushed on the valves margin drop and nuclear test-bed delays.

500252|2026-03.headline: LMW Q4 FY26 revenue rose to ₹854 crore (vs ₹789 crore a year ago) and TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore, with ~₹2,300 crore active.
500252|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue rose to ₹3,353 crore from ₹3,137 crore and consolidated profit to ₹195 crore from ₹151 crore, with standalone PBT up 42% to ₹221 crore. Q4 standalone revenue was ₹854 crore, up from ₹767 crore in Q3 and ₹789 crore a year ago. Management said textile machinery (TMD) order intake rose sharply in Q4 as cotton spinners' profitability improved, while the machine tool division grew strongly and ATC revenue reached ₹207 crore. Management flagged rising raw material, logistics and commodity costs across the industry, with no price hikes taken in MTD yet.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹767 crore in Q3 FY26 and ₹789 crore in Q4 FY25
vs ₹440 crore in Q3 and ₹493 crore in Q4 FY25
vs loss of ₹15.64 crore in FY25
one-time, related to new labour code and VRS outgo
vs ₹1,003 crore; ~10% foundry, balance machine tools
vs ₹146 crore; loss ₹32 crore vs profit ₹1.9 crore
vs ₹67 crore; breakeven vs loss ₹6.8 crore

segments.name: TMD (textile machinery)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,801 crore (down ~2%) and profit ₹9.75 crore; Q4 revenue ₹485 crore. Order book ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4. FY26 sales mix domestic:exports:spares 66:8:26.

segments.name: Machine tool division (MTD)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 25-28% in FY26 to ~₹1,205 crore for machine tools plus foundry (~10% foundry). Management cited ~11.5% margin in Q4 and no price hikes. Customer mix ~50-52% automotive, ~48% non-automotive; capacity headroom of ~20% and utilisation of 70-75%.

segments.name: ATC (aerospace and precision components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹207 crore (vs ₹169 crore); Q4 revenue ~₹56 crore with segment result ~₹11 crore (close to 20% margin). Order book ~₹360 crore to be executed over 18 months. About 90% of sales are exports; mix is ~78% metallics and ~22% composites.

segments.name: LMW Global and LMW China
segments.commentary: LMW Global FY26 turnover ₹184 crore with ₹32 crore loss and ₹44 crore order book. LMW China FY26 turnover ₹130 crore, breakeven, and ₹120 crore order book.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a much larger offtake of textile machines as cotton spinners' margins improve, but said it is too early to call a hockey-stick recovery like FY22.
ATC capacity additions are expected to start yielding higher turnover in the second half of FY27.
Management expects MTD margins to continue as turnover grows, and said it will invest for growth once utilisation nears 90%.
Management plans a new, larger ATC facility outside the city centre; ATC capex of about ₹150 crore over five years was referenced for infrastructure only, excluding machinery.
Management aims to rebuild exports to about 23-25% of sales over the next three years, from ~8% in FY26 (per the sales mix).
capex_capacity: Textile machinery capacity utilisation is about 50-55%; machine tool utilisation is about 70-75%, with ~20% headroom in MTD even after Q4 shipments.
Capex of over ₹300 crore was spent in the last three years, mainly for machine tool capacity and modernisation; about 50% of FY26 capex went to ATC.
ATC composites utilisation is about 50%, with headroom to grow.
ATC capex is project-specific and tied to order wins; the new facility is planned to be larger than the current one.
The company is considering an investment of up to US$30 million via a UAE holding company, partly for working capital and partly for export growth (GCC presence for two years).
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry has improved over the last two months, with good cotton yarn spreads, while crude-based synthetics face challenges. Demand is recovering from Bangladesh, China-linked yarn demand and Turkey.
TMD order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus the previous quarter's figure.
No price hikes taken in MTD; margin uplift attributed to operating leverage, with some forex income.
Raw material, logistics, steel, plastics and commodity costs are rising industry-wide; management did not disclose the size of planned price increases.
Import content in machine tools is about 50% of materials, mostly sourced locally in INR, with some USD-linked sourcing.
ATC is about 90% export-driven; customers are Tier-1 aerospace suppliers, and it also supplies ISRO, HAL and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the textile outlook and order pipeline, and the MTD growth and ATC order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Textile order book is ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4. MTD is continuing to grow with automotive at ~50-52%. ATC booked ₹195 crore; its order book of ~₹360 crore is to be executed over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is ATC's business, customer qualification cycle, and profit potential?
qa_highlights.answer: ATC has metallics and composites divisions covering engine parts, sheet metal, structures, assemblies and special processes. It is about 90% export-focused. Management said the ~19 certifications required include NADCAP, ISO and customer-specific ones. It does not disclose growth numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest up to US$30 million in a UAE holding company, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds are for working capital, which is under pressure because of geopolitics, and for export growth in GCC markets. It cited turning-centre exports of ~₹20 crore and a target of 23-25% exports over three years. No payback period was given.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROCE improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textile machinery is cyclical with an ~8-year cycle and the business is at a low point. It said ATC has much better ROCE, MTD will improve, and capex is heavy in textile. Management said it will keep investing through downturns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book 3,300 crore total with 2,300 crore active? What price hikes are needed to offset raw material costs, and what is the imported content?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: ₹3,300 crore total, ~₹2,300 crore active. Management would not share the size of price increases. Machine tool import content is about 50%, partly sourced locally in INR.

qa_highlights.question: Could ATC scale to ₹1,000 crore in five years, given a ~₹150 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹150 crore figure covers infrastructure only, excluding machinery, and that the new facility could scale beyond ₹300 crore of revenue. It did not give a ₹1,000 crore target.

risks_watch: Volatile crude and geopolitics are hurting synthetic fibre producers and pressuring working capital; banks may limit funding.
Raw material and logistics costs are rising, and availability is a concern (e.g., LPG and some industrial gases); pricing pass-through is unclear.
ATC order book depends on long-term contracts subject to push-outs or pull-ins, and the business is working-capital intensive because raw materials are imported.
Textile recovery may be cyclical and not a sharp rebound; management has not committed to a timeline.
Export contribution fell to ~8% of sales in FY26, against a historical 23-25% target.
500252|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on textile recovery timing and evasive on pricing, customer names, ATC targets and payback. It described the textile cycle as still at a low point.
key_quotes: We have actually got a significant increase in order book compared to the last quarter.
Whether this again would be, you know, a hockey stick recovery kind of what we have seen in 21-22 that is too early to be mentioned.
So, what you're seeing is pure operational the margin which is coming through because of consistently doing upwards of 100 crores or 300 crores per quarter.
But customer names and the projects would be difficult.

500257|2026-06.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.

Growth was broad-based across the US, India, Other Developed Markets, Emerging Markets and GIB, with ex-US organic growth above 20%. Management said Q2 onwards the US will moderate on Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, with quarterly US sales of USD 250-280 million, and it trimmed full-year EBITDA margin guidance to 24-25% from around 25%. Net cash fell to INR 2,831 crore from INR 4,636 crore after the VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 2,380 crore, up 13.9% YoY; diabetes grew 31.8% (1.8x category) and cardiac 1.2x category, while respiratory grew 6.9% vs category 11.3%. Chronic share rose to about 67% from about 65% in FY26; volume growth was 6.1%.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets (Europe, Canada, Australia)
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 1,149 crore, up 48% YoY, with Europe up 83% YoY. VISUfarma consolidation began this quarter. Management guides 10-20% growth over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 990 crore, up 52% YoY. Brazil grew 117% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin and Empagliflozin launches.

segments.name: GIB
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY in the quarter, per management; no further detail given on the segment's drivers.

500279|2026-09.headline: Onida Q2 FY27 brand revenue rose 65% YoY to Rs 150.4 crore, with brand margin at 17.7%.

H1 FY27 brand revenue rose 48% to Rs 325.7 crore and total revenue rose 25% to Rs 381.1 crore. Management said input cost inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, plastics, memory chips) squeezed sector margins, and it is relying on calibrated pricing, cost optimisation and mix to protect margins. Management guided to EBITDA breakeven at a gross margin of roughly 25-26%, but would not commit to FY27 EBITDA positivity.

segments.commentary: Portfolio being revamped; partly outsourced and partly made at Roorkee plant. E-commerce offering being completed.

500280|2026-03.headline: Century Enka Q4 FY26 operating revenue Rs 484 crore (+9% YoY) with EBITDA margin up 948 bps YoY to 11.46%, aided by price pass-through and some low-cost inventory.
500280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp YoY profit recovery: volume grew 14% YoY to 20,711 MT and EBITDA rose to Rs 55 crore, with price increases passed through after the Iran-related raw material spike from March. For FY26, revenue fell 15% to Rs 1,705 crore on 6% lower volume, but EBITDA (+29%) and PAT (+52%) improved. Management said the company has raised its indicative operating margin band to 7-10% from 6-8%, though it declined to guide quarterly numbers. Management indicated part of the gain came from consumption of lower-priced raw material, which will fade, and said the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex and renewable power additions will help margins only from H2.

500294|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 turnover grew 32% YoY to INR6,042 crore, the highest-ever Q2 revenue on a consol basis, and H1 turnover rose 21% to INR11,884 crore. Consol EBITDA margin was 8.79% in Q2 (8.66% a year earlier) and 9.1% for H1. Order book stood at INR80,167 crore at 30 September, up 11% YoY, with INR4,838 crore booked in the quarter and INR2,381 crore more in October. Management retained FY27 guidance (revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%, order inflow INR22,000-25,000 crore) but did not explain why H2 growth would slow, which drew sustained analyst questioning. Working capital eased, receivable days fell to 53 and JJM outstandings declined, while consolidated net debt rose to INR3,887 crore.

Bid pipeline unchanged at about INR2.5 lakh crore as shared in May; no segment-wise breakup given.
Retention money at INR2,547 crore (up about INR150 crore QoQ); contract retention 5%, up to 20% in some electrical contracts; can be partly replaced by bank guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why retain 8-10% FY27 growth after 21% H1 growth, implying a sharp H2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is for the full year, H1 was strong on mining and other projects, and Q3 is too early to comment; guidance was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retention money high relative to revenue, and can it be released?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer contracts carry 5% retention, some electrical contracts up to 20%, and CC road contracts in Mumbai high; retention will persist, with partial bank guarantee substitution possible on some contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the JJM payment improvement sustainable, and what is the outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM outstanding is INR2,246 crore; INR1,720 crore received in H1; JJM backlog excluding O&M is about INR5,412 crore, with UP legacy work largely done by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the unbilled revenue level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to EPC milestone billing and BharatNet and AP Capital City work drive unbilled; it is expected to remain at a similar level and to be realised progressively.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance for order inflow achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflow of INR11,108 crore including October is about 50% of the lower band; management retained the INR22,000-25,000 crore guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hyderabad investment of INR107-108 crore under construction?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an investment in a stalled Hyderabad project under NCLT and RERA proceedings; management said it is fully secured and not at risk of non-recovery, though timing is uncertain.

risks_watch: Guidance implies a sharp H2 slowdown: 8-10% full-year growth against 21% in H1 means H2 growth may be low or negative.
Consol net debt rose to INR3,887 crore (from INR3,513 crore at Q1); standalone debt INR2,471 crore; debt-equity 0.32.
