qa_highlights.answer: Q2 landed cost INR2.09 vs INR1.66 a year ago and INR1.95 in Q1; Q3 guided at about INR2.15-2.20 based on order pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 volume growth and industry demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand triggers are strong; industry growth 7-10% in Q2; Shree expects to grow slightly better than industry if demand holds at around 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Blended cost of production and pure cement cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended cost INR4,636 per tonne vs INR4,245 YoY and INR4,329 QoQ; pure cement cost not available, to be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Freight cost drop and whether one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by lower run-to-market, lean-season railway discounts and data-based freight fixation; management said there is no one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Trade vs non-trade mix and Meghalaya status?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade 61%, balance non-trade; Meghalaya protests cleared by state government, workforce and contractors mobilised, commissioning in FY28 still targeted.

qa_highlights.question: UAE volume outlook after new 3 mt mill?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 UAE volume about 2.1 mt; H2 similar; annualised UAE total about 4-5 mt after new capacity ramps (about 30% of 3 mt taken in first year).

500400|2026-03.headline: Tata Power Q4 FY26 PAT rose 8% to INR1,416 crores and FY26 PAT topped INR5,000 crores, with FY27 capex guided at about INR25,000 crores.
500400|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 EBITDA up about 10% to INR4,216 crores and PAT up 8% to INR1,416 crores, with full-year EBITDA up about 11% to INR16,090 crores and PAT above INR5,000 crores for the first time. Mundra was offline for nine months, and its SPPA with Gujarat is now signed, with four other states expected to follow in 4 to 6 weeks. FY26 capex came in well below the earlier guidance as transmission and right-of-way delays pushed projects out of the quarter. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR25,000 crores and about 2.5 GW of renewable commissioning, with roughly half of the 5 GW under-implementation pipeline due in FY27 and the rest by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up ~10% from INR3,829 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: Above INR5,000 crores (first full year above INR5,000 crores)

financial_highlights.metric: Solar cell and module manufacturing PAT (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: more than double the previous year

segments.name: Solar cell and module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR857 crores, more than double the prior year; plant stabilised with good yields. Captive demand from in-house utility-scale and rooftop projects is expected to absorb output.

segments.name: Odisha DISCOMs
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR809 crores vs INR439 crores in FY25. Management expects FY27 to be the best year for Odisha, with AT&C losses to fall about 2 percentage points a year to 12-13% over 4-5 years.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR499 crores with installations doubling; management targets 20% market share in 3 years and 50-60% rooftop market growth in FY27. Rooftop share was about 40% on 1.7 GW executed in FY26, per analyst.

segments.name: Utility-scale renewables / IPP
segments.commentary: Management expects about 2.5 GW commissioning in FY27 (solar 1.5-1.8 GW, remainder wind and hybrid/FDRE), with 5 GW under implementation, all in-house, and no third-party EPC work in FY27.

segments.name: Tata Projects
segments.commentary: Losses attributed to legacy projects (DFC and Barmer refinery), now largely complete. Management expects a return to profit in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai Transmission and IEL
segments.commentary: Q4 PAT lifts of about INR50 crores (Mumbai Transmission) and INR63 crores (IEL) were attributed to asset capitalisation and deferred tax; Mumbai Transmission adds about INR1,000 crores capex a year on a 70:30 debt-equity structure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex about INR25,000 crores, and similar capital outlay expected in FY28, covering solar, wind, pumped storage, pure hydro and transmission.
FY27 renewable commissioning about 2.5 GW (solar 1.5-1.8 GW), with a larger chunk from hybrid and FDRE projects.
Mundra SPPAs: Gujarat signed; remaining four states expected within 4-6 weeks; plant operating under Section 11 with billing per SPPA.
Odisha FY27 expected to be the best year yet, with AT&C losses falling toward 12-13% over 4-5 years.
Rooftop solar expected to grow 50-60% in FY27. Indian-made cell and module mandatory for government-subsidised rooftop from 1 June 2026.
Nuclear: 2 x 220 MW small modular reactor DPRs with NPCIL, some expected within about 6 months.

Current pipeline of 26.3 GW including existing capacity (16.7 GW operating): includes 2,800 MW Shirwata pumped hydro and Bhutan hydro (600 MW plus 1,125 MW, World Bank financing signed); Bhutan 1,125 MW expected around FY31-32.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR13,000 crores, below the guidance of about INR22,000 crores given in November; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays.
About 600 MW of large utility-scale projects being pushed to complete in Q1 FY27; deferred projects to be completed in FY27.
5 GW of renewable projects under implementation, all in-house; about 50% due in FY27 and the balance by FY28.
Company will not commission projects without permanent GNA and transmission certainty, which deferred some FY26 capex.
10 GW wafer and ingot plant to start in two phases, to supply Indian-made wafers from 1 June 2028.
Net renewable capacity: 16.7 GW operating; 26.3 GW including the current pipeline.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 2% in the last quarter but rose 5-6% from April; peak demand reached 256 GW and management expects it to exceed 270 GW in the next 1-2 months due to heatwave and El Nino.
Indonesian coal prices expected to stay within plus or minus 5%; coal and shipping costs have risen only slightly in the last two months.
Coal cost is a pass-through under the Gujarat SPPA, including FOB cost changes such as export duties or royalties.
Curtailment is intermittent and varies by location (evacuation allowed between 20% and 80%); cost reimbursed under GNA where curtailment occurs.
Solar and wind tenders: management says most of the current project pipeline bids with domestic cell and module requirements.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 capex well below the INR25,000 crore guidance from the November analyst meet, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance was closer to INR22,000 crores; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays. FY27 capex is about INR25,000 crores, with deferred projects completed this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full benefit of prior-period regulatory orders in Delhi distribution, and should FY27 reported numbers decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 regulatory approvals reflected INR783 crores vs INR333 crores in FY25. Further approvals are expected but are hard to quantify, as they relate to a pipeline of contested regulatory assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 IPP RE capacity addition and will the modules and cells be sourced in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 2 GW of commissioning in FY27, possibly slightly higher, of which solar is 1.5-1.8 GW. The in-house cell and module plant will supply the captive requirement, with about 1.4x module/cell content per MW.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the regulatory asset wind-down in Delhi is progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise the regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, which is under monitoring by the Supreme Court and APTEL.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tata Power sacrifice coal profitability under the Gujarat SPPA, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details will be shared once all five procurers sign, with no quantification given at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5 GW renewable pipeline represent installed or contracted capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is on installed capacity; contracted capacity is lower (about 1,200 MW for FDRE and hybrid wind per the slide cited by the analyst).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR250 crore deferred tax asset and the Q4 PAT lifts at IEL and Mumbai Transmission?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the deferred tax was recognised in Q4 based on better profit visibility and carry-forward losses. IEL uplift was from a plant commissioning; Mumbai Transmission's recurring uplift is from about INR1,000 crores of annual capex.

risks_watch: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual; slippage risk from transmission and right-of-way delays has already caused one shortfall.
Regulatory prior-period gains (INR783 crores in FY26) are lumpy and hard to forecast, so FY27 reported Delhi distribution profit could fall.
Four remaining Mundra SPPAs (states other than Gujarat) are not yet signed; billing is under Section 11 pending approvals.
Curtailment on solar projects and temporary GNA issues could hold back commissioning and PLF.
Coal monetisation remains open; management said a sale depends on valuation and signing all SPPAs.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA of 3.3x with a large capex programme; management says leverage discipline will be maintained.
Possible Indonesian coal export duty or royalty changes; coal cost is a pass-through under the SPPA.

Mumbai transmission adds every year INR1,000 crores of capex. So, on a 70-30, you will have a return on equity on 30%.

500400|2026-06.headline: Tata Power Q1 FY27 PAT rose 11% to INR 1,401 crore and EBITDA 8% to INR 4,249 crore, the 27th straight quarter of growth.
500400|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 1,401 crore (+11%) and EBITDA of INR 4,249 crore (+8%), with revenue also up. Q1 capex was INR 5,300 crore, a first, against a FY27 plan of INR 25,000 crore. Odisha DISCOM collections were delayed by government payment timing and a heatwave-related disconnection pause, which management says is timing-related. Renewable capacity additions were 226 MW in Q1, with about 500 MW near commissioning and a FY27 target of 2,500-2,700 MW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW.

financial_highlights.change: first time quarterly spend at this level

financial_highlights.metric: Rooftop revenue (Q1, per analyst calculation from slides)
financial_highlights.change: revenue roughly doubled YoY per management

segments.name: Renewables (generation)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 6.7 GW, with 2.5 GW to be added in FY27 and capacity expected to cross 9 GW by year-end. Q1 commissioning was 226 MW; 500 MW is described as ready within weeks, with Q2 commissioning of 800-900 MW targeted.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management guides to 60-70% growth this year. Q1 revenue was about INR 1,350 crore on 371 MW installed, and Mundra-style battery storage is being added. Management says cumulative rooftop revenue could reach INR 30,000 crore by 2029.

segments.name: Transmission (Mumbai and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Mumbai transmission has about INR 10,000 crore of regulated investment over five years. Two TBCB projects are near commissioning (Jalpura-Khurja now, Bikaner-Neemrana by October); TBCB revenue so far is construction-revenue booking, not line-by-line EBITDA.

segments.name: Distribution (Odisha and Delhi)
segments.commentary: Odisha PAT grew about 6% and units sold rose 10.4%, but collections were delayed by government payments, the heatwave disconnection pause and billing lag. Management says the DISCOM should be judged on a 12-month basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing (TP Solar)
segments.commentary: Module output crossed 1,000 MW in Q1 for the first time, while cell output fell after a line change. Margins are around 25-26%, and management expects yield and efficiency to peak in Q2.

segments.name: Tata Projects / solar EPC
segments.commentary: Third-party solar EPC has been discontinued and no new orders are being booked; remaining legacy projects are in final stages, and losses were booked in Q1. Management expects one more quarter of impact.

segments.name: Mundra (coal and power)
segments.commentary: Mundra's PAT rose on a higher share of coal profits, while EBITDA fell. The plant runs under a supplementary PPA on cost-reflective terms with no equity return. The state cabinet approvals are expected in August-September.

500405|2026-03.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR 1,587 crore (+3% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 253 crore at 15.9% margin; ABS running at ~65% of design capacity.

500405|2026-06.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,693 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.53%, while volumes fell 24.5%.
500405|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 1,693 crore, up 22% YoY, despite lower volumes, driven by higher raw material prices from the West Asia conflict. Operating EBITDA rose 88% YoY to INR 331 crore (19.53% margin) and PAT was INR 236 crore (13.96% margin), helped by wide global deltas between styrene monomer and downstream products. Manufactured volumes fell 24.5% YoY to 70,842 MT, with exports nearly absent and non-OEM demand down roughly 50%. Management declined to guide on volumes or margins, calling the situation fluid, and announced polystyrene and compounding expansions plus a new 80,000 TPA PS line totaling about INR 450 crore, funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the expanded compounding capacity to be used over 2-3 years after June 2027, with ABS compounds the main growth driver.

qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from wider global deltas, not volume; management called the level an aberration that will normalise over time and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Total capex about INR 900 crore, funded internally, and includes the 150,000 cubic metre wide-width board line.

qa_highlights.answer: Yes; freight rates are higher because Gulf voyages took 4-7 days, while alternate sources involve longer voyages and shipping constraints.

500405|2026-09.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to Rs 1,957 crore (vs Rs 1,100 crore) with EBITDA Rs 160 crore and PAT near Rs 95 crore, mostly price-driven.
500405|2026-09.overview: Standalone operating income for Q2 FY27 was Rs 1,957 crore against Rs 1,100 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of Rs 160 crore (8.12% margin) and PAT of about Rs 95 crore, nearly double. Management attributed the revenue jump partly to volumes and mostly to higher selling prices following raw material inflation. H1 FY27 operating income was Rs 3,649 crore, EBITDA Rs 508 crore and PAT Rs 331 crore (9.08% PAT margin), while H1 sales volume fell 3% YoY to 166,085 MT on weaker exports. The company remains debt-free with an investable surplus of Rs 886 crore and approved an interim dividend of Rs 2.5 per share (125%).

segments.commentary: Sales are seasonally low in monsoon months. A new wide-width line of 150,000 cubic metres is expected to start commercial production in Q1 FY28, with full absorption over 24 to 30 months.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from compounding of PS and ABS. Internal transfers of about 11,700 MT in H1 FY27 versus 4,300 MT last year lifted utilisation, and total volumes exceeded last year, though net market sales fell 2.8%.

500408|2026-03.headline: Tata Elxsi Q4 FY26 revenue INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency; EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 130 bps QoQ; FY27 growth guided to higher single digit.
500408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency, with transportation flat (+0.2% QoQ CC) and Media & Communications up 5.6% QoQ CC. Healthcare & Life Sciences fell 13.1% QoQ CC as expected deal awards slipped into Q1 FY27. EBITDA margin rose 130 bps QoQ to 24.6%, driven mainly by currency tailwinds (about 155 bps) partly offset by a salary increase (about 90 bps), with operating efficiencies adding about 65 bps. Management cut FY27 growth aspiration from double-digit to higher single-digit, with transportation expected to lead.

500408|2026-09.headline: Tata Elxsi Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR 1,055.7 crore, up 2.3% in constant currency; EBITDA margin 21.9%, up 70 bps QoQ.

Management attributed about 60-70 bps of the margin gain to currency and 10-20 bps to operating leverage and fading one-offs, which absorbed an annual wage revision. segments.commentary: Grew 3.4% QoQ in constant currency on ramp-ups of closed deals and AI-led wins, including a GenAI virtual assistant engagement with a global technology leader.

500410|2026-06.overview: Ambuja reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton at INR931. Management prioritised value over volume: total volumes fell about 7% YoY, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, and about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume in South was cut. Net operating cost fell INR206/t QoQ to INR4,241/t, which management says already absorbs about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost pressure. Management guides to 8% full-year volume growth (July trade volumes up 8% YoY) and FY27 cost of INR4,250/t, and expects some sequential cost pressure in Q2 that it says it can offset.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% FY27 volume guidance holds, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; it said market share was sustained or improved in trade while non-trade share was deliberately reduced.

500410|2026-09.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27: consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 MT volume; 14-project, ~30 MTPA expansion announced.
500410|2026-09.overview: Ambuja Cements (consolidated, including ACC) reported Q2 FY27 cement volume of 16.5 MT, revenue of INR9,197 crore, EBITDA of INR1,271 crore and PAT of INR236 crore, with the company stating it remains debt-free. Trade volumes grew 8.6% YoY and trade share rose to 74%, while B2B volumes were still negative, leaving overall volume roughly flat. Management announced 14 expansion projects adding ~30 MTPA cement and 10.3 MTPA clinker, costing about INR14,500 crore, and guided H2 volume growth above industry at a higher single digit. Cost per tonne was INR4,410 (INR4,182 normalised), with an FY27 target of INR4,250/t. The proposed merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja is now going to NCLT, with completion targeted within FY27.

500411|2026-06.headline: Thermax Q1 FY27: INR 91 crore cost-to-completion hit on a legacy government EPC project, plus ~INR 300 crore of unshipped inventory, drove a weak quarter with revenue up only ~7%.
500411|2026-06.overview: Management called Q1 FY27 the toughest quarter relative to expectations in recent years. The main drag was a INR 91 crore cost-to-completion charge on a legacy PSU/government project (original order ~INR 1,200 crore, taken in FY22), triggered by late engineering changes from the engineering partner in June. About INR 300 crore of finished goods, largely export shipments including Middle East, slipped out of the quarter due to high freight and customer deferrals, and commodity-linked cost increases of about INR 10 crore hit Industrial Products. Green Solutions lost about INR 20 crore at FEPL and carried about INR 8 crore of cost in Bio-CNG. Management reiterated that FY27 should be a good year, with the backlog (~INR 14,000 crore) and order inflow expected to exceed FY26, while acknowledging a credibility problem on execution and communication.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the legacy project behind the INR 91 crore hit, and how much remains to execute?
qa_highlights.answer: Original order ~INR 1,200 crore taken in FY22; the loss on the project is ~INR 150 crore in total. About 74% is invoiced and 26% remains. The engineering partner has confirmed its engineering is 100% complete; execution is over the next four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are government and PSU contracts a continuing risk, and do you have claims against the engineering partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the project a mistake and said the model (taking large PSU work with an outside engineering partner) will not be repeated. Government/PSU orders are now under INR 300-400 crore (<5% of backlog). They will only bid selectively where they have unique capability and can price the risk; one IOCL project (~INR 50-60 crore) and a Kandla green methanol project (<INR 100 crore) were cited.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top five people on the project had 20+ years at Thermax, and that talent was not the root cause. It said that gross project execution across >INR 100 crore projects adds to margin outside this one project. It acknowledged that surprises should be communicated earlier, though it did not commit to pre-announcing profit warnings.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 order inflow to exceed FY26. Drivers: a repeat supercritical project (at least one), Middle East and Africa international work, data centre cooling, waste-to-energy and captive thermal. Q1 handshakes worth a few hundred crore are pending advances.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are not 45-50%; they range 15-30% for most businesses. Slipped export items carried above-average margins. The US data centre shipment slips to Q3 recognition, while Q2 will see LD reversals and collections, and a large scheduled Q2 shipment is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will policy changes drive a significant pipeline, and in which segments?
qa_highlights.answer: The only policy change referenced is for Bio-CNG: a 20-30% price increase and blending mandates are expected around August (possibly at an August 10 conference). Green methanol tenders by SECI are also a potential driver. Thermal and cooling growth are not policy-dependent.

risks_watch: Completion of the legacy PSU project over four quarters; further cost escalation beyond the provision (LD exposure partly reserved).
Q2 Industrial Products margin pressure from steel and commodity costs; whether the ~INR 300 crore deferred shipments are fully recognised in Q2-Q3.
Order inflow recovery: the handshake orders need advances to be booked; the data centre and thermal pipeline must convert.
Bio-CNG policy announcement (price increase of 20-30%) expected around August; PGTR outcomes for remaining two projects in August and September.
Credibility: repeated gaps between guidance and execution; management said it would share surprises earlier but did not commit to profit warnings.
Chemicals margins: commodity pass-through and US tariffs; FEPL external investor process and Tamil Nadu regulatory approvals.
500411|2026-06.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution and disclosure, with an explicit acknowledgement that Q1 was the toughest quarter in years. Confident about FY27 orders, backlog conversion and Q2-Q4 profit recovery, but relies on promised policy, pipeline conversion and data-centre wins that are not yet booked; several answers were qualitative on margin and guidance.
key_quotes: A very difficult quarter, felt like was the toughest one, at least relative to expectations for the past few years that we have had, not that we haven't had tough quarters in the past, but this one felt particularly so.
And I would say even with taking this INR 91 crores hit, I expect this year to be a very good year.
So, I stay very bullish on orders and continuing to build a pipeline of the kind that we like and want to execute better on.
I think going forward, I'm not committing to it. It's between us as a team to decide, but I think this is something that we could have done.
It's not a quarter that we are proud of , nor is it reflective of what the company that we are building at Thermax and the performance that we can deliver at Thermax.

500413|2026-03.headline: Thomas Cook (India) Q4 FY26 group revenue fell 10% YoY to INR 17,707 million as Middle East war hit DEI and Desert Adventures, while Sterling and India operations grew.
500413|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 in two phases: the first nine months were relatively stable (top line up 7%, EBITDA up marginally), while Q4 absorbed the Middle East conflict, airfare spikes and rupee weakness, with the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor disruption earlier in the year. Full-year consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million (INR 85,578 million per closing remarks), but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million. India operations grew EBT 16% in Q4, and Sterling posted record Q4 numbers. The board approved in-principle demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, with a timeline of Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did financial services top line and EBIT drop, and is margin being traded for share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 forex EBIT rose 17% and FY EBIT held at about INR 149 crore; the drop reflects mix shift and net revenue reporting with franchise revenue shares, not margin pressure. Float of about INR 16 billion was flat vs December, which management read as customers not spending.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sterling EBIT been flat at about INR 129 crore for two years despite rising room count?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani cited the end of membership acquisition revenue, a 2-3 month ramp-up lag for new resorts, and upfront costs. Krishna Kumar cited high ROU depreciation from leased resorts. EBITDA margin was 31% and EBIT margin 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DEI loss behind us and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram said the corrections are not done and the cost base will reduce over 30-60 days notice periods. He expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end and said FY26 will not match original plans. Debasis Nandy said top line depends on ground conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash and deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said net cash is close to INR 800 crore, to be used for technology capex, repayment of long-term loans over the next couple of years, and inorganic growth if returns criteria are met. An analyst's build-up gave about INR 730-740 crore, which was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for Sterling and monsoon risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani said there are no headwinds so far in Q1; occupancy is expected to rise toward 65-70% over the year. Monsoon risk is being managed by asset protection and a geographically spread portfolio, with Q3 now the strongest quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said the process is on track for the 12-15 month plan, applications are with NSE and BSE, and completion is expected by Q1 FY28.

500413|2026-06.headline: Thomas Cook Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell 12% YoY to INR 21,530 million and PBT fell 21% to INR 885 million, driven by Middle East exposure.

Excluding the GCC subsidiaries, group EBIT grew 8%, and India businesses (forex, MICE, corporate travel, domestic) were stable to growing. Sterling Holidays reported its best quarter ever, with revenue up 21% and EBITDA up 21%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, though it said H2 should be better than H1 if conditions hold.

segments.name: Foreign exchange

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 17,106 million, -14% YoY; EBIT INR 405 million, -50%. Domestic +29%, short-haul +6% (+21% excluding Middle East), long-haul sales -28%. MICE +14% to INR 5,420 million; DMS -31% to INR 5,422 million with Desert Adventures revenue -89%.

segments.name: Sterling Holidays
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.7 billion (+21%), EBITDA over INR 620 million (37% margin), PBT margin 28% (+200 bps). Occupancy 77% (+700 bps), ARR INR 7,809 (+10%), RevPAR +20%; net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion.

segments.name: DEI (Digital Imaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,307 million vs INR 2,097 million; EBIT swung to INR -152 million from INR 106 million. About 50% of global business is in the Middle East; China site closures and Bahamas contract end added pressure. Net assets employed INR 243 crore.

segments.name: Desert Adventures (GCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 89% YoY; management estimated its EBIT impact at roughly INR 8-9 crore (about INR 90 million), not confirmed. Cost base did not flex as fast as volumes.

If conditions remain constant, H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1.

Sterling ARR +10% to INR 7,809 and occupancy +700 bps, indicating demand ahead of supply additions.
Short-haul ATV is 20-25% lower than long-haul, creating a mix headwind on revenue.
Management said margins are under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; tactical pricing used to keep capacity engaged.
TCS rate cut to 5% has had no visible impact on pricing; management called it a cash outflow, not a price change.

qa_highlights.question: How did underlying outbound leisure demand trend in July and early August, and do short-haul destinations carry comparable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July and early August conversion was better than Apr-Jun but too early to call a shift. Short-haul margins are similar to long-haul, though short-haul ticket values are 20-25% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thomas Cook pursue more airport forex counters over branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Airports are opportunistic, not a strategy; entry is made only at commercially rewarding terms, as with Delhi Airport.

qa_highlights.question: DEI: what are capital employed, normalised EBIT and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assets INR 243 crore; normal-year EBIT margin 6-7%; target 20% ROE. Major technology upgrade done, with periodic upgrades roughly every 10-12 years.

qa_highlights.question: Travel FY27 topline and EBIT margin outlook, and the TCS impact on pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance. Internal EBIT margin range 4-5%. Management said it saw no clear TCS pricing benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit earnings growth guidance still achievable, and what is the split of GCC subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm double-digit growth. DEI EBIT moved from INR 10 crore profit to INR 15 crore loss (INR 25 crore delta). Detailed numbers to be obtained from Investor Relations.

qa_highlights.question: Will DEI cost optimisation show in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visible benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27; revenue recovery in the Middle East will determine earnings quality.

risks_watch: Middle East exposure: DEI is about 50% of global business in the Middle East; April-June Middle East recovery was sub-20%, July about 30-35%. Revenue recovery is the swing factor for H2 earnings quality.
Desert Adventures cost base did not flex as fast as volumes; cost optimisation benefits at DEI are expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27, to be verified in the Q2 print.
No FY27 guidance; management could not confirm double-digit earnings growth, and the long-haul deficit (about 28-30% in Q1) must narrow further for H2 to beat H1.
Short-haul mix headwind: ticket values 20-25% lower than long-haul, and margins under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; Travel EBIT working range 4-5%.
Desert Adventures and DEI GCC-impact figures were not fully disclosed on the call (Desert Adventures EBIT impact about INR 90 million, unconfirmed); detailed split deferred to Investor Relations.
Geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia conflict) continues to drive customer booking hesitancy; July and early August conversion better than Apr-Jun but not yet confirmed as a trend.
key_quotes: Excluding the GCC-based subsidiaries, (DEI and Desert Adventures), the consolidated results of the group registered a growth of 8% at an EBIT level for the quarter, highlighting the resilience of our underlying businesses.
I really don't have an answer to say what will be my full year forecast at this point in time, given the environment which we operate in currently.

But just alluding to the point that I made previously to the question that was asked by Chetan, I think from a long-haul perspective, we are seeing some positive shift in the trend, that is, that whatever deficit that we were seeing previously, the deficit percentages have come down.
So honestly, to be very frank, I haven't seen a big impact coming out of the TCS.

500413|2026-09.headline: Thomas Cook India Q2 FY27 consolidated PBT before exceptionals held at INR 848 million (flat YoY) as income fell 5% to INR 20,030 million.
500413|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income fell 5% YoY to INR 20,030 million, but PBT before exceptional items was flat at INR 848 million and PBT margin rose to 4.2% from 4.0%. Financial Services was the standout, with revenue up 21% and EBIT margin at 44.1%. The India travel business recovered through the quarter, with the India EBIT deficit narrowing from 31% to 22%, while West Asia-exposed businesses (Desert Adventures, DEI, AlliedTPro) remained well below last year but improved sequentially. Sterling Holiday Resorts delivered its highest-ever Q2 revenue of about INR 1,272 million (+17%), with reported EBITDA diluted by a one-off-like GST input tax credit cost of about INR 40 million.

segments.name: Financial Services (Thomas Cook forex)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +21% with gross turnover INR 39 billion (+7%); EBIT INR 452 million, margin 44.1%. Retail turnover +12%, education forex +33% against a 34% fall in industry education remittances; corporate +10%, travel -6%.

segments.name: India Travel (B2C, domestic, DMS, corporate)
segments.commentary: India EBIT deficit narrowed from 31% to 22%; domestic B2C grew 8%, India DMS grew 16%, corporate travel revenue +11% to INR 446 million. B2C overall fell 17% on long-haul outbound weakness, with Kailash Mansarovar cancellations of INR 185 million.

segments.name: International DMS (Desert Adventures, AlliedTPro, Asian Trails)
segments.commentary: Desert Adventures sales down 67% (vs 89% in Q1); AlliedTPro down 22% (vs 40% gap in Q1); overall overseas DMS revenue -7%, Asian Trails +9%, South Africa private safaris +31%.

segments.name: Sterling Holiday Resorts
segments.commentary: Q2 room nights +23%, occupancy +300 bps, average rate +12%, RevPAR +12%; 7 resorts opened to 83 properties and over 4,000 keys. Q2 EBITDA hit by about INR 40 million GST input tax credit cost not present last year.

segments.name: DEI (Digiphoto)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 147 crore vs INR 130 crore in Q1 and INR 195 crore LY (about -22% YoY); EBIT loss of about INR 1.2 crore vs loss of INR 15 crore in Q1 and profit of INR 2.3 crore LY. UAE revenue back to 40-50% of prior year.

Desert Adventures expects about 50% recovery in the current quarter.
DEI expects a steady Middle East recovery and a much better Q3, its largest quarter, assuming no further disruption.
Sterling expects stronger revenue and earnings conversion in H2 as new resorts mature and GST cost comparability normalises from Q3.

500414|2026-09.headline: Timex Group India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% to INR359 crore and EBITDA 54% to INR66 crore, a record quarter, with product margin down 1.1pp.

E-commerce grew 75% to about INR190 crore, while trade grew 34% to about INR85 crore. Product gross margin fell about 1.1pp YoY on raw material inflation (copper, gold, silver), movement costs and a weaker rupee (USD near INR97 at peak), partly offset by an April price increase of 5-15% on selected SKUs. 500425|2026-03.headline: Ambuja FY26 volumes hit a record 73.7 Mt (+16%), but Q4 cost ran ~INR4,500/t and management reset FY27 guidance to ~80 Mt with capacity targets pushed out.
500425|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record volume year for Ambuja, with 73.7 million tonnes sold (up 16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (up 31%, INR887/t). Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above the INR4,000 exit target, driven by acquired-asset underperformance (Sanghi 57%, Penna 46% utilization), freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management reset its growth plan: FY27 volumes ~80 Mt (~8%), capacity target 119 Mt by end-FY27 (vs earlier 140-155 Mt), FY27 capex INR6,000-6,500 crore, and a cost reduction of about INR250/t in FY27 plus INR250/t in FY28. Pricing has not offset cost inflation, with April-over-March hikes of about INR10/bag in a few areas.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited stabilizing Sanghi and Penna plus about 10 Mt of new capacity commissioning between now and September 2026, which will be needed to reach 80 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook given the INR4,000/t exit target versus the reported INR4,500/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for March exit; the March month was about INR4,100/t normalized, and INR4,500/t is the peak. A reduction of INR150-200/t is expected from fly ash and green energy, and INR250/t is the FY27 average target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Ambuja's fixed cost rising faster than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher branding (about INR70/t for FY26), repairs and maintenance at acquired assets, freight, lower government incentives and higher heat consumption. Acquired assets were said to drag EBITDA by about INR70-80/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the reset of capacity and timelines a change in ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned but the timeline has moved; capacity was stepped back to 119 Mt by end-FY27. Capital will be deployed only after current projects are completed.

ACC's negative operating cash flow reflects receivables from Ambuja under the MSA, which are to be settled via an ICD.

rows.why: Sanghi at 57% (target 65-70%) and Penna at 46% (target 55-60%), with the turnaround running behind schedule and maintenance and breakdowns above expectations; targets are conditional on execution.

rows.label: Price pass-through limited
rows.why: Industry rose ~INR10/bag in March quarter, but management would be happy with half of any hike given weak demand, and realisation is ~INR254/bag, flat QoQ.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 10 Mt commissioning by September, the 18% IRR hurdle and cost levers (green power, fly ash), but candid that cost, capex timelines and acquired-asset utilisation under-delivered; analysts pushed on the FY27 volume target against flat Q4 volumes, cost versus the INR4,0

500425|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps QoQ), net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ; trade volumes -2% YoY.
500425|2026-06.overview: Management reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore, and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton of INR931 (grey cement INR911). Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management says is on track for the INR4,250/t full-year guidance despite about INR110/t West Asia-related inflation. Volumes fell sharply: total volume was down about 7% YoY, trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, as the company deliberately exited low-margin volumes, mainly in South and at acquired assets. Management guided to 8% trade volume growth for FY27 and said July trade volumes were up 8% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; FY27 guidance INR4,250/t

financial_highlights.value: down about 7% YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: trade share of sales 78% vs 74% prior quarter

financial_highlights.value: about 45 crore units; revenue about INR140 crore
financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26: about 24 crore units, about INR70 crore

financial_highlights.value: Lower in Q1 due to merger true-up; run rate to stay at Q4-level

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74%; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volume -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA cluster per management; trade volumes grew 2% YoY while low-margin non-trade fell sharply.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; Mumbai and Gujarat carry higher-margin non-trade volumes.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Deliberate exit of about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume; highest decline in the region. Trade sales only recently started picking up.

segments.name: Central / East
segments.commentary: Central: volumes declined as blended cement was pushed for margin. East: trade volumes sustained with healthy margins.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: RMC EBITDA about INR33 crore in Q1, versus margins of about 14-15% in the prior four quarters; management cited raw material pricing and lease accounting.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net cost guidance INR4,250/t, reaffirmed; management expects INR130-150/t of savings from initiatives, against a possible INR100/t rise in Q2 from geopolitical pressure.
FY27 trade volume growth guidance of 8%, with trade expected to be upwards of 75% of sales; July trade volumes up 8% YoY.
Capacity to reach about 119 Mt by end FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt), then 8-10 Mt of organic additions per year; FY28 capex in a run rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore.
FY28 green power share targeted at 60% (about 48% on combined sales-plus-consumption basis); RE capacity 1,122 MW by FY28.
Target cost of INR4,000/t or below by end FY28 (about INR250/t further reduction).
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt today; trial runs at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion) and Salai Banwa, UP (2.4 Mt) have started; Jodhpur (2 Mt commissioned, 3 Mt clinker trials) to stabilise in Q2 and be treated as commissioned in the September quarter.

Kalamboli, Mumbai (1 Mt) and Warisaliganj, Bihar (2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 (Warisaliganj likely September); Bhatinda (1.2 Mt) commissioned; Maratha clinker line moved to Q1 FY28; Mundra expected in about 18-24 months.
RE capacity 973 MW (about 1,122 MW target); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW; power cost reduced to about INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9.
About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily suspended for about six months; not permanent closure, per management.
Sanghi jetty and clinker expansion about INR600 crore; Penna AFR and WHRS investments INR100-150 crore; first coal block about 30 months away.
demand_pricing: Management said cement demand was stable in Q1, supported by infrastructure and housing; diesel shortages, packing material issues and East/West logistics disruptions hit Q1 volumes.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed this to Incoterm/ex-works changes and netting of certain channel costs, and said NSP is market-driven.
Analyst comparison: Ambuja NSP about INR100 below UltraTech's reported NSP in Q1, against an average premium of about INR50 over the prior quarters.
Management said Q2 net cost would be slightly better than the June-quarter level, after allowing for part of the geopolitical cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be muted in FY27 given the value-over-volume approach, and can lost Q1 share be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of 8% trade volume growth on July momentum (+8% YoY); it said share was sustained or improved in trade and was deliberately reduced in non-trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of green power sales and when will it be consumed in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; management expects about 50% consumed in Q2 (about 20 crore units). Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus green power savings, and at most 10% will be sold going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR206/t cost decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fly ash sourcing, RE power, clinker factor (down about 2-3%), logistics (-INR10/t) and fixed cost optimisation; gross savings were about INR316/t after absorbing INR110/t of West Asia inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up only marginally QoQ and below peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited accounting netting of certain expenses against NSP, ex-works Incoterm effects, and a Q1 disruption; it expects NSP to move in line with industry.

qa_highlights.question: Acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi, Orient): what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Orient at 87% utilisation with minimal investment; Penna needs about INR100-150 crore and a channel push in the South; Sanghi investing INR600 crore in a jetty and improving utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Ambuja-level ICD given to the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as part of the MSA arrangement, with Ambuja supplying about 3 Mt of cement to ACC; the ICDs are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, and merger is in advanced stages.

risks_watch: Trade volumes still negative YoY in Q1; the 8% FY27 growth target implies a steep ramp (about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months per analyst math).
Q2 cost pressure from geopolitical escalation (possible INR100/t rise); clinker and coal inventories give about one month and three months of cover respectively.
Suspended capacity (about 3.5 Mt) and South volume exits (about 1 Mt); restart timing and the impact on fixed-cost absorption remain open.
Maintenance cost accounting: management is still engaging auditors on spreading O&M cost across four quarters; Q1 reflected actuals.
Green power consumption depends on grid connectivity for some plants, expected in two to three quarters; RMC margin fell to about 7% from 14-15%.
500425|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on cost and capacity delivery, with specific numbers for savings and commissioning, but noticeably defensive on volume decline and NSP gap versus peers, attributing both to one-off disruptions and accounting netting. Several answers on ICDs, RMC margin, cost reconciliation and the Orient valuation were deferred offline.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
And I would not shy highlighting that we are already seeing an 8% improvement on the trade volumes.
Having a sustainable performance matters more than anything.
Yes, you might be leaving the volume, but you're not leaving value on the table.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ, is on track for INR4,250/t FY27 guidance, with INR130-150/t of further savings expected against a possible INR100/t Q2 geopolitical rise; EBITDA/t INR931 vs 16.7% margin up 331 bps QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity moves from 109 Mt to about 119 Mt by end FY27; Jodhpur 2 Mt commissioned (September quarter), Kalamboli 1 Mt and Warisaliganj 2.4 Mt due Q2, with Dahej 1.2 Mt and Salai Banwa 2.4 Mt already in trials.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 8% trade volume growth for FY27 with July trade up 8% YoY, but Q1 trade was -2% YoY and total volume about -7%, so the back-nine-months ramp of about 12-13% is steep and capacity utilisation is only about 65%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 65% with about 10.2 Mt of capacity already being added to reach 119 Mt, so a fresh capex push is not indicated; FY27 capex is held at about INR6,500 crore and FY28 run rate INR6,000-7,000 crore is already planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the INR4,250/t cost, 8% volume and 119 Mt capacity guidance without raising it, and flagged a possible INR100/t Q2 cost rise from geopolitical pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade volume was -2% YoY in Q1 and the 8% FY27 target needs about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months, while Q2 cost could rise by INR100/t and about 3.5 Mt of ACC capacity is suspended.

rows.label: NSP gap versus UltraTech narrowing
rows.why: Ambuja NSP is about INR100/t below UltraTech in Q1 versus an average premium of about INR50 earlier, and management says NSP is market-driven and expects it to move in line with industry.

rows.label: ACC intercompany loan (ICD) repayment under merger
rows.why: ICDs to the parent are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, with about 3 Mt cement supplied to ACC under MSA, but the treatment was deferred offline.

rows.label: Green power self-consumption and RE build-out
rows.why: About 50% of 45 crore units sold in Q1 expected to be consumed in-house in Q2 (about 20 crore units), power cost down to INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9, and RE capacity 973 MW rising toward 1,122 MW by FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost savings (INR4,250/t guide, INR130-150/t more savings) and commissioning dates, but defensive on the volume decline and the NSP gap to UltraTech; analysts pushed on the steep 8% volume ramp, NSP discount and RMC margin fall to about 7%, and several items were deferred

500425|2026-09.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27 consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 Mt volume; 14 expansion projects add ~30 Mt grinding, capex INR14,500 crore.
500425|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 cement volume was 16.5 Mt, revenue INR9,197 crore, EBITDA INR1,271 crore (about 14% margin, INR770/t) and PAT INR236 crore, with the company still debt-free. Trade volumes rose 8.6% YoY and trade share reached 74%, while non-trade (B2B) volumes remained negative, leaving total volume roughly flat. Management announced a 14-project expansion (about 30 Mt grinding, 10.3 Mt clinker) costing about INR14,500 crore, taking capacity to 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30. Unit cost fell to INR4,410/t (INR4,182/t normalised), with FY27 target of INR4,250/t reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 fuel cost INR1.66/kcal; Q2 FY26 INR1.60/kcal
vs INR6/unit in Q2 FY26 and INR4.3/unit in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Trade (consol)
segments.commentary: Trade volumes up 8.6% YoY; trade share up to 74%; premium products 37% of trade sales (35% last year). West trade volume +14%, North +13%, South +13%, Central +9%, East flat.

segments.name: Non-trade / institutional (B2B)
segments.commentary: Deliberately recalibrated to drop negative-EBITDA volumes; still negative YoY in Q2, with management expecting positive growth in Q3 and Q4. Blended cement share 82% of sales vs 77% a year ago.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Quarterly volume 1.07 million cubic metres, up 19% YoY, from a network of about 125 plants; RMC EBITDA margin about 7% per management.

segments.name: Green power / fly ash
segments.commentary: Green power sales about INR136 crore (352 million kWh) in Q2, booked in other operating income; fly ash revenue about INR25 crore. Combined contribution about INR97/t per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cost target of INR4,250/t reiterated; management says ~INR160/t improvement is needed in H2 and that it is on track, subject to no further global fuel escalation.
H2 FY27 volume growth guided to be ahead of industry, at higher single digit (aim for double digit) against industry growth of about 6-7% for FY27.
Capacity to reach 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30; FY28 cost target of INR4,000/t for combined existing and new capacity.
Capex: about INR14,500 crore for the 30 Mt programme (~INR7,500 crore a year over the next two years). FY27 capex guided at INR6,500-7,000 crore, with INR3,000-3,500 crore in H2.
Merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja to go to NCLT; completion expected within FY27 and described as EPS accretive.
Realisation: INR10/bag price increase realised in October; further hikes expected. Management sees about INR150/t benefit from trade mix by June 2027.
capex_capacity: Q2 commissioned 4.6 Mt at Dahej (Gujarat), Salai Banwa (UP) and Kalamboli (Maharashtra); 3.2 Mt at Bathinda (Punjab) and Penna Jodhpur (Rajasthan) stabilised with ramp-up in H2; 2.4 Mt at Warisaliganj (Bihar) due Q3 FY27.
Expansion: 30 Mt grinding (West 15.2 Mt, East 11.6 Mt, North 2.9 Mt) and 10.3 Mt clinker (Maratha 4 Mt, Umrangso 4 Mt, Mundra 2.25 Mt).
Execution timelines of about 14 months for grinding units and about 18 months for integrated units; equipment reportedly already ordered and PMC appointed. Around 20 Mt bunched into March-May 2028.
Penna and Sanghi utilisation about 50% in Q2; company-level utilisation about 61-62% in Q2, targeted at about 75% by end FY27.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt with clinker factor about 66%. Debottlenecking at about four plants with Loesche expected to complete in 4-5 months.
demand_pricing: Price held at INR255/bag in the monsoon-hit Q2; INR10/bag realised in October with more hikes expected.
Management says the trade-led push adds about INR40/t so far, rising toward INR150/t by June 2027.
Demand headwinds: weak monsoon with drought declared in several large states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra, Rajasthan); impact expected with a lag in Q3-Q4.
Brand equity claimed to support a price premium, backed by independent surveys. Competition in East and West expansion regions acknowledged; management says 'there is a market for everyone'.
Fuel: blended fuel cost INR1.87/kcal in Q2 vs spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal; domestic coal above 60% of mix, imported under 40% (pet coke about 10-12%).

qa_highlights.question: Why revisit expansion now when H1 volumes were negative and demand soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly performance did not drive the decision; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the second wave (West, East, North) is value-accretive, mostly brownfield and clinker-backed. Earlier guidance of 140 Mt by FY28 and 155 Mt by FY30 is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex needed to reach 149 Mt, and how will debt evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR14,500 crore for 30 Mt, roughly INR7,500 crore a year. Management described the programme as self-sustainable from cash flows, with only interim debt possible.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost guidance of INR4,000/t: does it include new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000/t target for FY28 covers the combined existing and new capacity at 149 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in execution given past delays and bunched-up commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lessons from the first phase, including a contractor issue, and a tighter scheduling plan with 14-18 month build cycles. It did not name specific suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 volume growth and Q3 cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 volume growth is guided to higher single digit, aiming for double digit, ahead of industry. The cost path is supported by green power, BCFC, WHRS (18 MW at Sanghi in Q3) and AFR.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to the proposed merger and the tax shield from Penna and Sanghi, which it said is one driver of EPS accretion.

risks_watch: Execution risk: about 20 Mt of capacity bunched in March-May 2028 on 14-18 month build cycles, with prior contractor issues.
Cost risk: fuel costs rising (spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal vs blend INR1.87); FY27 target depends on INR160/t H2 improvement and no further escalation.
Demand risk: drought in major states may moderate construction with a lag; non-trade volumes still negative.
Utilisation of acquired Penna and Sanghi assets at about 50% in Q2; management withheld detailed figures until Q3-Q4.
Merger completion via NCLT and EPS accretion claims; Q2 tax rate unusually low on merger-linked tax shield.
Management's previously stated 'aggressive' vs 'calibrated' expansion framing was questioned by analysts and left unresolved.
500425|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on cost, trade growth and the expansion roadmap, but defensive when pressed on why capex is accelerating after weak H1 volumes. Management was evasive on specific numbers (Assam capex, Penna/Sanghi utilisation, spot fuel) and deferred several details to later updates.
key_quotes: So this is nothing as per any sense of change. We are now following our defined pathway, which we had guided before.
Closer to INR14,500 crores will be what we require for this 30 million tons, which has a combination of IUs and GUs.
As a going -- running company, we are giving INR4,000 combination of existing and new.
So we had a program of INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores for this year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Unit cost fell to INR4,410/t (INR4,182/t normalised) with FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated, needing ~INR160/t H2 improvement; trade mix benefit seen at ~INR150/t by June 2027 vs ~INR40/t so far, though spot imported coal at INR2.80-2.85/kcal vs blended INR1.87 is a risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2.4 Mt Warisaliganj due Q3 FY27 and 3.2 Mt Bathinda/Penna Jodhpur ramping in H2; the 30 Mt grinding and 10.3 Mt clinker programme (~INR14,500 cr) is approved, with 14-18 month builds and ~20 Mt bunched into Mar-May 2028.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 volume growth at higher single digit (aim double digit) vs industry 6-7%, backed by trade volumes +8.6% YoY and trade share at 74%, though non-trade volumes remain negative and drought is a lagged headwind.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 30 Mt grinding and 10.3 Mt clinker programme (~INR14,500 cr) was announced this call; FY27 capex guided at INR6,500-7,000 cr with ~INR7,500 cr a year over the next two years, and utilisation at only ~61-62% means no further near-term capex announcement is needed beyond execution.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: INR10/bag hike realised in October with more expected, and trade mix benefit rising toward INR150/t by June 2027, but drought in several large states and weak H1 volumes cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 cost target of INR4,250/t needs ~INR160/t H2 improvement with fuel escalation a risk (spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal vs blend INR1.87), and drought impact on demand is expected with a lag in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: ACC and Orient merger into Ambuja via NCLT
rows.why: Merger to go to NCLT with completion expected within FY27 and described as EPS accretive; Q2 tax rate was low on the merger-linked tax shield from Penna and Sanghi.

rows.label: Penna and Sanghi utilisation ramp to ~75%
rows.why: Penna and Sanghi at ~50% utilisation in Q2 with company-level utilisation at 61-62% targeted at ~75% by end FY27, but management withheld detailed figures until Q3-Q4.

rows.label: FY28 cost target INR4,000/t
rows.why: Management targets INR4,000/t for FY28 across existing and new 149 Mt capacity, supported by green power, WHRS (18 MW at Sanghi in Q3), BCFC and AFR, though execution risk on bunched commissioning remains.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost, trade growth and the expansion roadmap but defensive on why capex is accelerating after weak H1 volumes; analysts pressed on execution risk from bunched commissioning, Penna/Sanghi utilisation and the aggressive vs calibrated expansion framing, which went unresolved

500440|2026-03.headline: Hindalco Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore on Oswego fire, but adjusted PAT rose 10% to INR5,796 crore.
500440|2026-03.overview: Consolidated business-segment EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR10,812 crore, while reported PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore due to exceptional items including the Novelis Oswego plant fire. India business segment EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR6,610 crore and PAT rose 11% to INR3,549 crore. Copper EBITDA hit a record INR907 crore on higher by-product (sulfuric acid) realisations, while Novelis adjusted EBITDA was about $498 million ($543/t). Management expects Novelis to recover in FY27 as Oswego hot mill restarts and Bay Minette ramps.

segments.name: India aluminium upstream
segments.commentary: Shipments +2% YoY, revenue +11% YoY, EBITDA INR5,448 crore at $1,756/t. Q4 cost rose about 2.4% QoQ; Q1 FY27 guided about 5% higher, mainly furnace oil.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream
segments.commentary: Shipments 124 KT (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR255 crore (+16% YoY), $226/t, driven by volume, mix and premiumisation.

segments.name: Copper (India)
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA INR907 crore (+48% YoY) on by-product realisations and efficiencies; metal shipments 128 KT (-5%), CCR volumes 91 KT (+11%).

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 917 KT (-4% YoY) excluding 73 KT Oswego loss; adjusted EBITDA $498 million ($543/t). Impacts: $53 million Oswego fire, $27 million tariffs, offset by $41 million Sierre flood insurance recovery.

guidance_outlook: Novelis: Oswego hot mill to restart in the next few weeks; current-year headwinds expected to substantially recover in FY27; long-term $600/t EBITDA target intact.
Novelis cost programme: FY26 exit run-rate savings raised to $200 million (from $125 million target); 3-year structural cost cut of $350-400 million by FY28 exit.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield plant: cold mill commissioning started, hot mill commissioning from next month, commercial coils in FY28, 18-24 month ramp; start-up costs of about $100-150 million annually expected below EBITDA.
India copper TC/RCs: more than 85% contracted at benchmark; expected close to zero or slightly negative for FY27.
India copper EBITDA: Q1 FY27 similar to Q4 (INR900 crore range) but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3.

India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crore (later framed as INR15,000-17,000 crore for the next year); Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, mainly Bay Minette; consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over next 2 years; net leverage around 2x.
Aluminium market: deficit now 1.5 million t for CY26 (from 0.3 million t), tightest in Q2-Q3 CY26.
Renewable capacity 470 MW at year end, rising to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Aditya smelter: first 180 pots by December 2027, next 180 pots by December 2028; management says timelines look firm.

Captive coal: Chakla box cut expected in next 2 months, first coal possibly Q4 FY27; Bandha box cut done but first coal only in FY28 due to high strip ratio; Meenakshi (strip ratio under 1) expected to add substantial volumes in FY29; Chakla Stage 1 forest clearance received.

Downstream: Aditya FRP ramping up; battery enclosure at full ramp-up; Aditya battery foil commissioned; Taloja AC fin facility commissioning; specialty alumina precipitate hydrate commissioned, under customer approval.

Copper: inner grooved tubes (35 KT) in customer qualification; 50 KT Pakhajan e-waste recycling plant to commission in August; copper smelter about 3 years out; battery grade copper foil scaled down to a smaller capacity in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices strengthened in the quarter; West Asia conflict disrupted supply; global market now seen in 1.5 million t deficit for CY26.
India Q4 FY26 aluminium demand about 1.6 million t, +9% YoY; India copper demand 402 KT, +10% YoY.
Q4 FY26 hedges: aluminium 64% at INR2,807/t; currency 26% at INR88/$. FY27 hedges: aluminium 29% at $3,013/t; currency 14% at INR90.13/$.
Sulfuric acid prices high due to Middle East conflict and China export restrictions; management expects Q1 FY27 to be slightly above Q4 but could correct if Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Global concentrate TC/RCs at record lows around -$0.21 to -$0.25/lb; expected to stay negative through FY27.
Alumina sales 211 KT in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 guided at about 170 KT.
Midwest premium at about $380/t due to 50% US tariffs; Japan premium up on supply tightness and freight. Domestic vs export realisation gap narrowed; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q4 copper EBITDA reflect the full sulfuric acid price surge, and how sustainable is the INR900 crore run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 expected in the same range given high sulfuric acid, but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3 and cautioned that Hormuz reopening could correct sulfur prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India and consolidated capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India FY27 capex about INR12,000 crore, rising to INR15,000-17,000 crore in the following year; Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, falling sharply in FY28 after Bay Minette. Consolidated capex expected to be lower than current levels; FY28 detail deferred to Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt breakdown and peak?
qa_highlights.answer: India gross debt INR12,200 crore, cash INR18,000 crore (net cash INR6,000 crore). Novelis gross debt INR75,000 crore, cash INR11,000 crore (net debt INR63,000 crore). Consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over the next 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is $600/t Novelis EBITDA assuming current scrap spreads and start-up costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management does not assume current spreads or metal prices; start-up costs sit below EBITDA. The $600/t target is seen as sustainable, not reliant on current tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How do coal captive mines change costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chakla and Bandha expected at similar cost to market coal; Meenakshi substantially lower. Captive mines expected to flatten the cost curve over 15-20 years; meaningful captive volumes only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis avoid shipping to Canada given tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is mitigating tariffs by using US cold mill capacity, including additional capacity secured at Logan; Kingston (Ontario) mill longer-term planning still pending.

risks_watch: Oswego hot mill restart timing and the resulting Novelis volume recovery in Q1 FY27.
Tariff exposure (Midwest premium, US-Canada flows) and possible relief from governments.
Input cost inflation: Q1 FY27 cost guided about 5% higher, driven by furnace oil; CP coke and pitch also rising.
Sulfuric acid and TC/RC normalisation could reduce copper EBITDA from the current run-rate if Hormuz reopens.
Captive coal ramp-up delays (Bandha high strip ratio) and Aditya smelter timelines.
Net debt rising toward INR80,000-90,000 crore; net leverage target around 2x.
