segments.name: Feminine Care
segments.commentary: Category growing 7-10%, with growth coming from varied sub-segments; Whisper is the market leader. Whisper Period Panties sold over 10 crore units and tripled the business in FY26 (as stated); Whisper Nights is about half of pad users' choice and growing ahead of the category.

segments.name: Personal Healthcare (Vicks)
segments.commentary: Category growing about 2-3%, volatile through the year and linked to monsoon timing. Vicks VapoRub returned to double-digit growth within 6 months of its all-night relief relaunch. Vicks Cough Drops offtake growing double digits this year, with volume and volume share up on a past-3-month basis.

guidance_outlook: Management expects some near-term challenges to continue, citing macro headwinds, West Asia conflict and inflation.
Feminine hygiene category expected to grow at late single digits this year; long-term category growth expected at mid to high single digits.
Multi-year savings master plans being built for each business unit, intended to fund reinvestment and margin expansion.
Management said it would not guide on price-sensitive matters; no quantitative FY27 sales or margin guidance was given.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were disclosed on the call.
Manufacturing footprint and future investment plans were raised in Q&A but were not answered.
demand_pricing: Crude and resin prices have risen 30-50% due to the West Asia conflict; the company said it has not gone out of stock.
Rural consumption still exceeds urban, but a softening trend is visible due to inflation; non-food inflation is below the RBI 4% medium-term target.
More than 50 new players have entered feminine hygiene in the last 10 years, including regional and D2C brands.
Healthcare category has declined for many quarters post-COVID, with early signs of recovery in recent quarters.
Qcomm: one in four consumers buying period products are choosing panties, where Whisper is #1.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth slowed over the last 5 years despite ad spends, distribution expansion and launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fast-changing consumer needs, shifts in media and retail, and very high competitiveness; it said it is investing in innovation, communication and Nights and Panties segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not launching new-age products in feminine hygiene?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to its Nights and Period Panties launches and upgrades to existing lines across benefits and sizes, with Whisper Period Panties positioned as the segment leader.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins being optimised at the expense of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said flat sales came after reinvestment and that savings are used to fund product, package and demand generation; green shoots are visible in focus portfolio areas.

qa_highlights.question: How are West Asia-linked cost pressures being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude and resin prices are up 30-50%, supply continuity has been maintained, and savings programmes are being accelerated to offset costs.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on CEO/CFO turnover and management tenure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategy has stayed constant across leadership changes and that a grow-from-within talent model ensures succession continuity.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on buybacks, parent company investment and manufacturing expansion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to answer, citing unpublished price-sensitive information.

risks_watch: Top-line stagnation: FY26 sales flat despite investments; watch whether volume growth returns in FY27.
Commodity and resin cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, which could erode the margin gains.
Intensifying competition from regional and D2C players in feminine hygiene and healthcare.
Monsoon timing affecting healthcare category growth.
CFO transition effective July 1, 2026 (Srividya Srinivasan) and leadership change narrative.
Softening rural and urban consumption from inflation.
500459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on strategy and productivity but cautious on near-term demand; management openly acknowledged flat sales and category challenges. It was evasive on guidance, buybacks, capex and manufacturing expansion.
key_quotes: We know that the results have been mixed.
Our Integrated Growth Strategy is working for us.
Whisper Period Pants has sold 10 crore units in the last year!
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock or made compromises on product performance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Structural operating margin improved about 1 pp in FY26 and Rs 86 crore of savings were delivered, with multi-year savings master plans being built, but crude and resin prices are up 30-50% from the West Asia conflict and could erode gains.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 sales were flat at about Rs 4,300 crore and feminine hygiene category is expected to grow late single digits this year, with Whisper Period Panties tripling; volume recovery is not guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were disclosed; manufacturing questions were declined.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No quantitative FY27 sales or margin guidance given, and management flagged near-term challenges continuing from macro, West Asia conflict and inflation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects near-term challenges to continue, and resin and crude costs are up 30-50%, with healthcare category growing only 2-3% and monsoon-dependent.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Whisper Nights and Period Panties upgrades across benefits and sizes are cited as ongoing proof points, and Vicks launches were discussed, but no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Savings master plans per business unit
rows.why: Rs 86 crore of savings delivered in FY26 and multi-year master plans are being built for each business unit to fund reinvestment and margin expansion, with savings being accelerated to offset resin costs.

rows.label: Vicks VapoRub and cough drops recovery
rows.why: VapoRub is back to double-digit growth within 6 months of relaunch and cough drops offtake is growing double digits, but healthcare category is only 2-3% and monsoon-timed.

rows.label: CFO transition July 1, 2026
rows.why: Srividya Srinivasan takes over as CFO on July 1, 2026, with management saying strategy has stayed constant across leadership changes.

tone.note: Management was confident on strategy, savings and Whisper/Vicks proof points but cautious on near-term demand and costs, and evasive on guidance, buybacks, capex and manufacturing; analysts pushed on flat sales, growth slowdown and new-age product gaps.

500463|2026-03.headline: Black Box targets INR12,000 crore organic plus INR6,000 crore inorganic revenue by FY30 (~$2bn), with 10% EBITDA margin; order book ~$800m.
500463|2026-03.overview: This was a Capital Markets Day held June 1, 2026 (transcript filed June 7), not a quarterly earnings call, so no Q4 FY26 quarterly P&L was presented beyond FY26 annual figures. Management said the turnaround is complete and set a FY30 target of INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, 17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore) plus ~INR6,000 crore (~$0.7bn) from acquisitions. FY26 EBITDA was INR570 crore at a 9% margin, up from 4.3% in FY23, and the order book reached ~$800m. Growth is pinned on hyperscale data centre fit-out, enterprise GSI services, the TPS products business (~$90m to $200m) and rest-of-world, including India.

financial_highlights.change: Expanded by 470 bps (as stated; likely margin expansion context)
From INR269 crore and 4.3% margin in FY23
Up from ~$500m; ~60% growth cited; $1bn booked in FY26

financial_highlights.value: Over 9x growth in last three years

financial_highlights.change: Total capital raised ~INR600 crore in the period

financial_highlights.value: Receivables up ~INR580 crore QoQ; payables up ~INR300 crore; receivable days ~90+ vs 60-75 normal
financial_highlights.change: Driven by 38:62 revenue skew to March quarter

segments.name: Hyperscale data centre / GSI
segments.commentary: Data centre share of order book ~25%, guided to rise to 35-40% in coming quarters. Seven dedicated sites for one hyperscaler (three more allocated); GSI headcount ~1,500, with 400 in data centre practice and 2,100 hires planned in 12 months, mostly in the US.

segments.name: Technology Product Solutions (TPS)
segments.commentary: Current business ~$90m, targeted at ~$200m by FY30 with ~40% gross margin and a 10% EBITDA target. Seven verticals addressed, ~$3bn TAM; R&D in Bangalore and Limerick, Ireland; flagship product line Emerald.

segments.name: India / Rest of World
segments.commentary: India is 6-7% of revenue (~$50m), targeted at 8-10% of a $2bn business (~$200m). India is a low-margin geography per management; 300+ partnerships and 17 offices / 35 delivery centres cited.

segments.name: Financial services (anchor client)
segments.commentary: A large US bank client has been served for 27 years at ~$100m annual spend, ~$1bn lifetime revenue crossed in the last 10 years, 68% growth since 2016.

guidance_outlook: FY30 target: INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, ~17% CAGR) plus ~INR6,000 crore inorganic (~$0.7bn), totaling ~INR18,000 crore (~$2bn). Computed at INR95/$.
EBITDA margin: 10% overall target, reached in FY27 per management (9% currently); FY30 EBITDA margin target of 10%+.
Order book expected to reach $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings); average order age 15-18 months.

Acquisitions: ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year, targeting 2-5% EBITDA margin targets bought at 6-8x and turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; 70% upfront, 30% earn-out. Brazil (2S) acquisition recently announced.
Debt-to-equity could rise to ~1:1 after the acquisition programme; otherwise debt to stay broadly flat with internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Data centre workforce: 2,100 hires planned in next 12 months (mostly US) to go from ~4,000 total employees to ~7,000.
GCC in Bengaluru to grow from ~600 to ~1,000 people.
Centralised resource management in Plano, Texas; estimating tools Accubid and P6 Primavera; separate project controls team.
Training: 600 people trained on AI; 36 hours of learning per person per year vs 28-hour industry average; 1,500 certifications in data centre business.
Capital allocation priorities: people and training, AI-enabled platforms, working capital, and acquisitions in Europe, APAC, India and Latin America.
demand_pricing: Management says demand outweighs supply in data centre work; prices have 'considerably increased', with cost increases passed through; margins claimed to improve modestly with execution.
Mike Carney stated no business is won on price; win depends on execution and relationships.
Hyperscaler data centre contracts: mainly time-and-materials / design-build; ~25% of project value is unknown at outset; change orders agreed, e.g. ~$2.5m change orders on a $10m initial scope.
US skilled labour market is constrained; inflation expected. Talent on Tap programme trains trade-school hires (~3 weeks) to address it.
Management claims ~0.2% share of the $200bn networking and connectivity opportunity; India data centre market from 1.3 GW to 8 GW (42% CAGR), India IT $171bn (9.2% CAGR per Gartner).

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory for non-TPS businesses, and how acquisitions will be funded (~$200m a year).
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 10% EBITDA across all businesses; management expects to reach 9% to 10% in FY27 with scale. Acquisitions funded mainly by internal accruals plus some debt; ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of hyperscaler exposure in order book and margin difference vs enterprise.
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres ~25% of order book, rising to 35-40%. Margins are stated as not varying by customer type; India is a low-margin geography and data centre operators/multi-tenants carry higher margins than general contractors.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure for data centre projects (time-based vs fixed price).
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of annuity contracts, fixed-price small projects and cost-plus for large multi-year projects; management says 15-20% of projects are expected to convert to annuity as the business scales to $2bn.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising and receivable outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: The March quarter revenue skew (62% in March vs 38% in first two months) raised receivables by ~INR580 crore; management expects receivable days to revert to 60-75 from ~90+ as the skew normalises to 45:55.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring split by geography and rupee sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: The 4,000 headcount is ~2,000 US, ~1,200 India (500-550 India business, balance GCC), ~300 Europe, ~400 Latin America; hiring is revenue-based and the US accounts for most growth. Plan computed at INR95/$; currency moves affect INR revenue, margin percentages unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to the FY30 plan.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited talent and attrition, unforeseen events and geopolitics; said currency is naturally hedged (earn and spend in same currency) and the main risk is project execution.

risks_watch: Execution on large, multi-year data centre projects where ~25% of value is unknown at start and scope changes are common.
Talent: 2,100 US hires in 12 months in a constrained labour market; wage inflation and attrition.
Working capital: receivable days at ~90+ and the March-quarter revenue skew; watch normalisation toward 60-75 days.
Acquisition integration and the INR6,000 crore inorganic target, funded partly with debt; D/E could rise to ~1:1.
Tax rate normalising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years, which will weigh on PAT.
Order book conversion: target of $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 and new hyperscaler wins.
500463|2026-03.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with aspirational targets described as a 'dream' and 'plan A'. Specific numbers are given for FY30 and order book, but several claims (market sizes, share, margins) are loosely supported and the Q&A on margin, tax and funding was answered in detail.
key_quotes: So, this is our organic plan, primarily the aspiration to go to INR12,000 crores from current INR6,000 crores, almost like doubling that to a $1.3 billion revenue.
We are expecting that when we end this fiscal year, which is March '27, our order book will remain in the range of probably $1.3 -1.4 billion.
Without a hyperscaler being there, it won't happen, because they are the anchor tenants for most of the GPU data centers.
The focus now is the execution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 9-10% EBITDA in FY27 from 9% in FY26 (INR570 crore), with TPS targeted at 10% EBITDA and acquisitions turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; margins are claimed to improve modestly with execution.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to add 2,100 data-centre/GSI hires over 12 months (about 4,000 to 7,000 employees) and grow Bengaluru GCC from ~600 to ~1,000; this is headcount capacity, not plants, and no utilisation was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book ~$800m is guided to $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (50%+ growth), and FY30 organic revenue target is INR12,000 crore (~17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the plan is headcount and acquisitions, with no utilisation disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book growth guided at 50%+ in FY27 and the Brazil acquisition is adding inorganic revenue, but no revenue guidance raise was given and the FY30 targets were newly set at the Capital Markets Day.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivable days at ~90+ versus 60-75 normal, a 2,100-person US hiring push in a constrained labour market, and the tax rate rising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years all weigh on PAT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TPS flagship product line Emerald is a named product line with a target of $90m rising to $200m by FY30, but no specific launch date was given.

rows.label: Order book to $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027
rows.why: Order book grew from ~$500m to ~$800m with $1bn booked in FY26, and management guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise to 60-75
rows.why: Receivables rose ~INR580 crore QoQ on a 62% March-quarter revenue skew, and management expects the skew to normalise to 45:55, but this depends on the skew changing.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity could rise to ~1:1 on acquisitions
rows.why: D/E fell from 1.2 to 0.6 (debt ~INR800 crore, equity ~INR1,300 crore), but ~$200-250m of acquired revenue per year is to be funded partly by debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY30 targets, order book growth and 10% margin in FY27, and detailed on margin, tax and funding; analysts probed margin trajectory, working capital and acquisition funding, and management called the targets a plan A.

500463|2026-06.headline: Black Box Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 38% to INR160 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR7,800-8,000 crore.
500463|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% YoY, margin 9.3%, up 90 bps) and PAT of INR56 crore (+18% YoY). The quarter included about two months of consolidation from the Brazilian acquisition 2S, which contributed about INR60 crore. Order bookings were US$339 million and the order backlog reached about US$950 million (up 83% since the transformation began). Management reiterated FY27 guidance, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9.3-9.4%, and said growth would be weighted to H2 and spill into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up 83% since start of transformation; company said up 83% YoY in opening remarks

segments.name: Hyperscale / data center
segments.commentary: Management expects hyperscale to grow about 25% in aggregate across the business, with data center tenures of 24-36 months. A new US hyperscaler order of US$131 million (about INR1,240 crore) was added, with work on site starting from November.

segments.name: Non-hyperscale enterprise
segments.commentary: Expected to grow at modest double-digit, about 10%, lagging the hyperscale cycle, with enterprise spend expected to follow with a lag.

segments.name: Product business (TPS / KVM, Emerald)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making at EBIT level as revenue grows; management expects about 20% growth in FY27 and says the segment is highly accretive once scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR7,800-8,000 crore (+23-27% YoY).
FY27 EBITDA INR725-750 crore (+27-32% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps). Medium-term aim is 10% or more at scale.
FY27 PAT INR300-325 crore (+38-50% YoY).

FY27 order bookings US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +32-45% YoY); order backlog at March 31, 2027 of US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +65-75%). Management said the backlog figure may be conservative and gave updated detail after Q2.
Tax rate expected at 10-15% in FY27 and FY28, normalising to about 20% thereafter.
Operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Long-term aspiration of INR18,000 crore (US$2 billion) revenue by FY30: about INR12,000 crore organic and INR6,000 crore inorganic.
capex_capacity: Plan to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support execution.
Large hyperscale sites are gigawatt-plus; deployment and hiring for the new US hyperscaler order start only from November.
Talent and people investment described as largely done; cash flow expected to turn positive from operations.
Management said supply chain, particularly cables and fibre, improved over the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Management says competition is based on execution capability, scale, and the ability to deploy skilled resources, not on lowest price.
Management estimates the addressable opportunity at US$250-300 billion, with about 60-70% of spending in the US.
Management says the company has executed several hundred megawatts, close to a gigawatt, and is now receiving more invitations to bid (pull rather than push).
Data center orders are described as accretive to margin, and expected to be more accretive at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic revenue growth given 2S was included from May?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said INR60 crore of the INR1,719 crore came from 2S, and the balance is organic. June quarter is seasonally weak for 2S.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow improve given the investment needs suggested by the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said talent investment is largely complete, operating cash flow should be positive, and cash flow should rise with growth. Working capital still needs funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative, given backlog growth ex-long-term projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said most backlog execution falls in Q3 and Q4, and it will spill into FY28. FY27 growth is about 22-25% and FY28 growth should exceed that. Backlog could end higher as new orders come in Oct-Mar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for non-data center businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said non-hyperscale enterprise is expected to grow about 10%, with a lag behind the hyperscale cycle. Overall growth is about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will TPS / product business reach profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the product business is expected to grow about 20% in FY27 and focus on mission-critical products such as KVM/Emerald. Losses should narrow with scale.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance imply depressed Q2/Q3 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said Q4 should be at or above 10%. Investment in training and talent means guidance is kept at 9.3-9.4% for the year, with 10% or more expected at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from hyperscaler capex moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said current pipeline shows new projects being announced and no slowdown in conversations. Shifts between sites would be absorbed across multiple geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO cited scale, execution capability, customer relationships, and the ability to fund and train staff. He said competition will exist, and the company is aiming to take share.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on H2 conversion: Q1 was described as seasonally soft, and FY27 growth requires about 30-40% sequential or YoY growth in H2.
Margin: management is holding guidance at 9.3-9.4% because of talent and training investment, and 10% is targeted only at scale.
Customer concentration in hyperscalers: any capex moderation or site delay would affect execution and backlog timing.
Product business (TPS) still loss-making at EBIT level.
Working capital and cash conversion needs to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Tax rate is currently low due to carried-forward losses; it is expected to rise to about 20% after FY28.
Transcript notes that several guidance figures were corrected on the call (backlog, bookings, EBITDA, PAT, margin); use the corrected figures stated in the call.
500463|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and backlog, with explicit caution on margins (guidance held at 9.3-9.4% because of investment in talent) and on H2 execution timing. Management relied on the backlog to support the FY27 numbers and gave limited detail on cash flow and on the product business.
key_quotes: We are in the midst of one of the largest digital infrastructure investment cycles in history.
Winning these engagements is no longer simply about offering at the lowest price. It is about demonstrating consistent execution on mission -critical infrastructure.
Our medium-term objective remains to consistently operate at or above a 10% EBITDA margin while maintaining healthy returns on capital.

Historically, quarter 1 has been a relatively softer quarter for Black Box. We expect stronger revenue conversion and operating leverage in the second half of the fiscal year with this momentum supporting the delivery of the FY27 guidance outlined in our presentation.

But I think it's better to factor in what we are planning to invest and therefore, guiding where Deepak had guided at about 9.3%, 9.4% (inadvertently stated - 9.4% to 9.5%: to be ignored) at this time.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps) and said Q4 should be at or above 10%, with 10%+ targeted at scale.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical plant capacity is discussed; growth is via onboarding nearly 2,000 professionals and deployment of a US$131m (about INR1,240 crore) hyperscaler order starting November, so new people capacity rather than plants is what comes online.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record INR1,719 crore revenue (+24% YoY), US$950m backlog and US$339m Q1 bookings, with FY27 revenue guided +23-27% to INR7,800-8,000 crore and growth weighted to H2 and spilling into FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held backlog and bookings guidance and kept margin at 9.3-9.4% with explicit caution on H2 execution timing, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue of INR7,800-8,000 crore needs roughly 30-40% H2 growth after a seasonally soft Q1 that included only about INR60 crore from 2S, and margin is held at 9.3-9.4% because of talent investment.

rows.label: US$131m hyperscaler order starts work in November
rows.why: The new US hyperscaler order of US$131m (about INR1,240 crore) has work on site starting from November, with hiring for it starting then.

rows.label: Backlog and bookings guidance for FY27
rows.why: Order bookings guided at US$1.3-1.4bn and backlog at US$1.3-1.4bn by March 2027, with management saying the backlog figure may be conservative and most execution in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive as talent investment completes
rows.why: Talent investment described as largely done and operating cash flow expected to turn positive, but working capital still needs funding and no cash flow number was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on hyperscale demand, backlog and the US$131m order, and cautious on margins held at 9.3-9.4% for talent investment and on H2 execution timing; analysts pushed on organic growth ex-2S, backlog conservatism, cash flow and the loss-making product business.

500469|2026-03.headline: Federal Bank posted record quarterly net profit of INR 1,145 crore (up ~10% QoQ) in Q4 FY26, with CASA crossing INR 1 lakh crore and GNPA at a decade-low 1.62%.
500469|2026-03.overview: Federal Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR 1,145 crore, its highest ever quarterly profit, on underlying metrics excluding one-off gains. Growth was led by commercial banking, gold, LAP and CV/CE, while CASA and NRE deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore each. Asset quality hit decade-best levels, and a one-time INR 456 crore interest gain from an income tax refund was used partly to build a floating provision ahead of ECL transition. Management declined to revise its credit cost, growth or cost-to-income guidance, and said the ECL impact is still being assessed.

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% QoQ and ~26% YoY, described as primary growth engine.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Grew 9% QoQ and 26% YoY, despite downsizing a sub-segment for regulatory alignment; around 14% of advances, LTV below 54%.

segments.name: LAP
segments.commentary: Expanded 8% QoQ; management expects growth to accelerate.

segments.name: Agriculture and microfinance
segments.commentary: Agriculture grew 5% QoQ; microfinance grew 7.28% QoQ, restarted in small way last quarter.

segments.name: CV/CE
segments.commentary: Sharp uptick of 8.5% QoQ.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% YoY; deliberately calibrated to protect yield and portfolio health.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional banking
segments.commentary: Essentially flat QoQ; deliberate credit selectivity toward high-rated counterparties.

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Growing ~23% YoY; growth skewed to transactors rather than revolvers.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost guidance of 50-60 bps retained, not revised; FY26 credit cost was about 56 bps; management said it will reassess once ECL impact and West Asia situation are clearer.
Cost-to-income guidance range of 53%-56% retained; management said it has done slightly better than guidance in FY26.
Further deposit repricing benefit expected in Q1 and early Q2 FY27; NIM expansion expected from mix, not only repricing.
About 100 branches planned for next year after 39 added in Q4 FY26.
Medium-term CASA ratio target of 36% reiterated as achievable; no numeric loan growth guidance given.
ECL transition impact still being assessed; draft guidance indicates the floating provision can be used during transition.
capex_capacity: 39 new branches added in Q4 FY26; slower branch addition in H1 FY26 due to network study and rebranding.
About 100 branch additions planned for FY27.
Branch network restructuring and relocation to improve productivity of existing branches.
Wealth management business launched during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Retail home loans: unattractive pricing (15-year at ~7.15%); bank not pushing volume, which weighs on overall retail growth; retail book flat YoY.
Wholesale deposits reduced during the year; retail term deposits growing faster than system.
Remittances remain elevated; management sees no change unless significant job losses in UAE.
Corporate: targeting early double-digit growth, focus on mid-market (about 75% of NTB acquisitions) and cross-sell.
Competition described as intense and sometimes irrational in rate-setting.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on loan and deposit growth after balance sheet realignment; staff cost decline and one-time provisions treatment.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CASA and retail term deposit growth exceed system and wholesale deposits fell; no numeric FY27 guidance, only said traction is building. Staff cost impact not quantified. Floating provision is for ECL transition and not linked to any specific asset.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and whether deposit repricing is done.
qa_highlights.answer: Some deposit repricing left into Q1 and early Q2 FY27. NIM down only about 2 bps over FY26 on full-year basis. Day count impact present in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and ECL impact on provisions and credit cost.

500470|2026-03.headline: Tata Steel FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 35% YoY to Rs 34,848 crore; FY27 cost savings target Rs 7,100 crore and capex step-up to ~Rs 20,000 crore.
500470|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 63,270 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,953 crore (16% margin), helped by higher India realisations, volumes and cost savings. India EBITDA grew 17% YoY to Rs 34,272 crore at a 24% margin, and UK plus Netherlands EBITDA turned positive for the full year. Management guided Q1 FY27 realisations up about Rs 6,000/t in India, £80/t in UK and €80/t in Netherlands. The main overhang is the Netherlands coke and gas plant (CGP) closure, which has led auditors to flag a material uncertainty on TSN's going concern, plus a delayed UK EAF grid connection.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of closing the Netherlands coke and gas plants and buying coke?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a cost penalty from losing coke oven gas and adding freight, partly offset by lower CO2; net impact depends on timing, with coke sourced from India or elsewhere. No quantified figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did auditors flag material uncertainty on TSN going concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cause is a post-balance-sheet letter from environmental agencies on intent to revoke permits without dates or pathway; closure must be planned and safe, and CGP shutdown is expected to take time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK EAF commissioning delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay of 6-8 months or more after plant build; initial estimate of 18 months has come down to about 12 months, with efforts to reduce further and trials planned with one line connection.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited optionality to reach 45-50 Mt on existing sites, a new approach of announcing projects only after FEL3 and approvals, and a shift of value pools to downstream amid rising iron ore and coal costs.

qa_highlights.answer: TMILL stake rises from 51% to 74% with NYK holding the balance; TMILL has ~55 rakes and about 80% of revenue from ground and rail logistics. Slurry pipeline and waterways expansion planned.

500470|2026-06.headline: Tata Steel 1QFY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, up Rs 2,400/t YoY; India margin 27% despite lower volumes and a Netherlands DSP shutdown.

500472|2026-03.headline: SKF India Q4 FY26 sales rose 3% QoQ to INR 5.55 bn, but PBT margin fell to about 9% after Q3 one-off gains; management guides 11-12% PBT margin.
500472|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) sales were a record INR 5.55 bn, up about 3% QoQ and about 14.8% YoY, driven by cars, 2-wheelers and powertrains, with a drop in distribution. Profit before tax margin fell to about 9% as Q3 had one-off gains from forex, fixed-deposit interest and employee cost provision reversals. FY26 sales grew about 12.7% to INR 20.3 bn with OE up about 20%, while full-year PBT margin fell to about 12.3% on demerger costs, mix and discounts. Management pointed to 11-12% PBT margin as the near-term sustainable level and said cash conversion was about 85%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 8% of Q4 sales; broadly steady but slightly lower. Domestic demand is prioritised given limited capacity, and overseas demand is served from nearby plants.

500472|2026-09.headline: SKF India Q2 FY27 sales rose 16% YoY to about 2% QoQ growth, but EBITDA margin fell to about 14.5% as steel and supplier price increases ran ahead of customer price pass-through.
500472|2026-09.overview: Management said sales grew 16% YoY and 2% QoQ, driven mainly by volume with marginal price or mix impact. EBITDA improved 155 bps YoY but fell 255 bps QoQ, as COGS rose from steel inflation and value-addition price increases given to suppliers. Customer price increases were agreed in some cases but not yet billed because purchase order amendments were pending, and management expects most recovery in the December quarter. Management also presented a new global brand identity and a hybrid-transmission EV bearing win from a major Indian OEM, with SOP around Q2 2028.

segments.name: Vehicle aftermarket (VA)
segments.commentary: Share of 19% in Q2 and 20% in H1. Volumes down about 7% YoY in Q2, similar to Q1, with management describing the decline as stabilised but margins still under pressure across hundreds of customers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Share of 10% in Q2 and 9% in H1. Management guided to a range of around 10% of sales going forward, with quarterly variation from one-off transactions.

guidance_outlook: Price increases from customers are expected to be largely recovered in the December 2026 quarter, with a possible marginal spill-over into Q4 FY27.
Management expects EBITDA margin to return to the earlier guidance, which it said is above 15%, within FY27, not deferred to FY28.
Volume growth of 15% or slightly above is considered reasonable for FY28, with some new capacity replacing trading volumes and some revenue growth from price increases.

Export share expected to hold around 10% of sales.
capex_capacity: One new production line starts in the December 2026 quarter; another channel with capacity enhancement at Haridwar goes live around March 2027, and a third new channel comes from July 2027.
Traded goods imports are very small. Trading from SKF Industrial, which began after the demerger, is expected to decline to negligible levels over the next couple of years.
Ceramic bearings are made in India; the ceramic ball is a purchased component. The hybrid transmission programme starts production around Q2 2028.
Haridwar investment is capacity expansion for EV-specific bearings, mainly anchoring two-wheeler traction motor bearings; management said it will not monetise backward integration separately.
demand_pricing: Macro: GDP projected at 7.35% for the last quarter; CPI around 4.9%; manufacturing PMI 55.1 in September 2026; automotive production rose across all categories in the quarter.

Pricing: steel inflation and supplier value-addition price increases from April were absorbed in Q2. Customer price increases were partly agreed, with some effective January or July, but purchase order amendments were pending, so billing slipped.
Aftermarket competition: management said pricing pressure from hyper-competitive players has abated and margins are stabilising, but further action is needed.

Passenger vehicle programmes are tied to CAFE III norms. BS-7 discussions are at development stage with commercial vehicle customers, with high-efficiency product nominations expected around end-Q2 2027.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give percentages. It said a large part should materialise in the December quarter, and some customers had earlier price increases effective January.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin should be viewed excluding other income, but the company-level view should include it, since rental from SKF Industrial space would be redeployed to SKF India's own production.

qa_highlights.question: Are the other expense increases linked to demerger costs?

500477|2026-03.headline: Ashok Leyland FY26 revenue hit INR44,007 crore (+13.6%) with Q4 EBITDA margin at 14.6%; management flags steel-led commodity pressure in Q1 FY27.

Q4 revenue was INR14,161 crore (+19% YoY) and EBITDA INR2,066 crore (14.6% margin), though operating leverage was weak due to performance bonus provisions. Management said Q4 gross margin improved 80 bps despite commodity headwinds, helped by ~1% price hikes in January and value-engineering/e-sourcing savings. Outlook is cautious: May demand is holding, but diesel availability and steel costs are the main near-term concerns for Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a range for FY27 industry growth in a downside case?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to estimate. It said demand is resilient, and any Q1/Q2 dip could convert to pent-up demand in Q3/Q4. Q1 FY27 is expected to be better than Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Cross-functional teams are reviewing opex line by line for savings. Recovery is possible only partly; if commodity costs rise sharply, the margin impact will be significant.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no operating leverage in Q4 on staff and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Performance bonus provisions for executives were booked only in Q4, after thresholds were met, and commodity costs also rose. Q4 gross margin still improved 80 bps QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY28 (Saudi plant, 18-24 month original timeline, under eval
rows.why: A new Saudi plant is being evaluated for acceleration, but no firm date is given; RAK is being restored from 600 rated to 800 units a month, which is recovery of existing capacity rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic MHCV industry grew 13% in Q1 with June and July above 20%, and management guides high single-digit MHCV growth from October; Ashok Leyland's domestic MHCV volume was 22,998 units (+15%) and exports should recover as RAK ramps to 800 from 600.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was INR900-1,000 crore a year in the last two years, Q1 capex was INR153 crore, and management said capex will keep rising over the next 2-3 years with a detailed plan to follow.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is conservative on H2, guiding only high single-digit MHCV growth from October against a high base of 20-21% growth in October 2025, and flagged Q2 as the margin-challenged commodity peak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said Q2 commodity costs will be higher than Q1 and margins will be challenging; the deferred inventory cost will flow through later and MAV competition is rising, while the high base could slow H2 MHCV growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited HIPPO, TAURUS and the air-suspension MAV launches to improve mix in Q2, and the air-suspension truck offers 4 tonnes of extra payload versus 2 tonnes from a competitor.

rows.label: Switch Mobility e-bus order book about 2,100 after 650-unit win
rows.why: A 650 e-bus order lifted the order book to about 2,100, with 225 e-buses delivered and close to 300 e-LCVs in the quarter.

rows.label: Optare debt repayment GBP 25 million a year
rows.why: About GBP 50 million of Optare debt remains, with GBP 25 million planned for repayment this year and GBP 25 million next year; net cash rose to INR2,252 crore, up more than INR1,431 crore YoY.

rows.label: HLF-NDL Ventures reverse merger awaiting NCLT approval
rows.why: The reverse merger is pending NCLT approval, and management says HLF's capital structure cannot be disturbed before the merger; HLF PAT was INR123 crore (+37%) on AUM of INR60,310 crore (+20%).

tone.note: Management was confident on volume recovery (June and July industry above 20%, record Q1 domestic LCV offtake) and cautious on margins, calling Q2 the commodity peak and challenging; analysts' questions focused on the margin headwind, mix, MAV competition and the HHF investment ahead of the demerger

500480|2026-03.headline: Cummins India FY26 sales rose 18% to INR11,950 crore and Q4 PBT before exceptionals rose 20% to INR820 crore, with data centres at about 35% of Q4 domestic power gen revenue.
500480|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 18% YoY to INR11,950 crore, with domestic sales up 19% to INR9,961 crore and exports up 12% to INR1,989 crore. Q4 FY26 sales were INR2,963 crore, up 23% YoY but down 1% QoQ, and PBT before exceptional items rose 20% YoY to INR820 crore. Power generation domestic sales led growth, while industrial domestic sales were flat for the year. Management guided to moderate growth across segments in FY27, citing caution on geopolitics, commodity inflation and supply constraints despite robust domestic demand and order books.

segments.name: Power Generation domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR4,758 crore, up 24% YoY. Q4 sales INR1,294 crore, up 48% YoY and 21% QoQ; Q4 split was LHP INR55 crore, medium range INR177 crore, heavy duty INR108 crore, with the balance high horsepower.

segments.name: Distribution domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR3,278 crore, up 22% YoY. Q4 sales INR766 crore, up 21% YoY but down 18% QoQ. Management said price contributed little to growth.

segments.name: Industrial domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,650 crore, down 1% YoY. Q4 sales INR381 crore, up 1% YoY and down 18% QoQ; Q4 split was construction INR164 crore, rail INR111 crore, compressor INR59 crore, with the rest mining and defence.

segments.name: High horsepower exports
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR984 crore, up 20% YoY. Q4 sales INR217 crore, down 1% YoY and 7% QoQ.

segments.name: Low horsepower exports
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR807 crore, up 3% YoY. Q4 sales INR127 crore, down 18% YoY and 5% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Management expects moderate growth across segments (power generation, industrial, distribution) in FY27, but did not quantify it.
Domestic demand is described as robust, with inquiries and order book strong, though management is cautious on geopolitics, commodity prices and inflation.
Exports: Europe and Asia Pacific growing modestly; Middle East and other markets weaker; no change in outlook.
Data centre engine mix expected to stay QSK60 for the next 2 years; QSK78 seen as more likely than QSK95 for larger sizes.
No major capex planned; continued spend on line modernisation and output expansion, following more than INR1,000 crore invested over the last 5 years.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 70% across combined power gen and industrial facilities.
Capex has been ongoing for 10 years, focused on modernising lines and raising per-line output; no major capex plan announced.
Parent investing about $450 million to add 20 GW capacity by 2030, mainly for data centre engines; management expects this to shorten import lead times over time.
Lead times for imported large data centre engines have risen over the last few years due to global data centre demand; no figures given.
High horsepower order lead time is 3 to 6 months. Data centre orders typically come 6 to 12 months before site readiness, with revenue recognised on installation.
No local supply chain yet for BESS; management is working on it.
demand_pricing: Data centres were about 30-35% of FY26 domestic power gen revenue and about 35% in Q4; data centre inquiries have risen sharply since October 2025, from both hyperscalers and colocation players.
Hyperscaler revenue in Q4 was about INR250 crore, per management's answer to a Citi question.
Non-data centre power gen grew at higher double digits in FY26, with demand from manufacturing (solar cell, pharma), quick commerce dark stores, and luxury residential and commercial realty.
Power gen pricing is largely holding after the CPCB IV+ transition, though price competition continues in very low-cost lower ranges.
Industrial: railways and mining order books are building; compressor enters a down cycle; road construction is moderate.
Commodity inflation is being passed on with a lag; DEF is a very small part of distribution, so impact is limited.
Competition in HHP and data centres is intense but unchanged in intensity, per management; competitors are importing 95-litre engines.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 and Q4 power gen revenue came from data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres contributed 30-35% of FY26 domestic power gen revenue and about 35% in Q4. Distribution revenue for data centres sits on top of that and was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 hyperscaler revenue disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crore of value in the quarter, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will larger engines (QSK78/QSK95) change the competitive landscape and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: QSK60 remains the near-term product for the next 2 years, and QSK78 looks more likely than QSK95. Management said no competitor makes 95-litre engines in India, and its value proposition covers service and solutions beyond cost, so margin impact is hard to call.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the commodity impact and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity increases are passed on with a lag. Order-book timing creates the challenge. DEF is a very small part of distribution. HHP lead times are 3 to 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity expansion planned, given 70% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex is planned. Management is spending on line modernisation and output increases, and can tap global parent plants via an integrated supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest and inquiries are high, but there is no sales pipeline yet and no local supply chain. Management is not sharing a contribution estimate or customer cohorts.

qa_highlights.question: Is price or volume driving growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is volume-led. Price and content gains apply mainly to CPCB IV+, and distribution growth comes from new solutions, not price.

risks_watch: Margin mix: data centre and CPCB IV+ growth relies on related-party QSK60 engines and imported QSK95 engines; management says margins are not affected, but it is an open question.
Commodity inflation and supply constraints (labour at suppliers, fuel costs, transport disruption from the war) may hit margins on existing orders, with pricing pass-through lagging.
Competitive pressure from imported large-engine players and local competitors in data centres, and price competition in low-end power gen.
Export demand is uncertain due to geopolitics; Middle East and other markets are weaker.
Distribution growth may slow as CPCB IV+ units leave warranty from June 2026, though management expects extended warranty packages to offset this.
Q4 FY26 sales were down 1% QoQ, and distribution and industrial fell sharply QoQ.
500480|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the trajectory of data centres and power gen, with the outlook for FY27 qualified as moderate. Management is cautious about commodities, geopolitics and supply constraints, and evasive on quantities (lead times, BESS contribution, currency effect on exports, extended warranty revenue booking, and distribution revenue for data centres).
key_quotes: So the inquiry velocity definitely increased quite a lot since October last year, and we continue to see that, Mohit.
For now, no major capital expenditure plan.
Pricing is largely sustaining across the range.

rows.why: CPCB IV+ units leave warranty from June 2026, which may slow distribution growth (Q4 distribution sales INR766 crore, down 18% QoQ), though extended warranty packages are expected to offset this.

rows.label: Export recovery
rows.why: Export sales fell 6% YoY in Q4 to INR450 crore; Middle East and other markets are weaker, with only modest growth in Europe and Asia Pacific.

tone.note: Management was confident on data centres and power gen demand and order books, but cautious on FY27 (only unquantified moderate growth), commodities, geopolitics and supply constraints, and evasive on lead times, BESS contribution and data centre distribution revenue; analysts probed margin mix from

500480|2026-06.headline: Cummins India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR3,375 crore, but pre-exceptional PBT fell 0.7% to INR721 crore as commodity inflation hit margins.
500480|2026-06.overview: Net sales hit a record INR3,375 crore, up 18% YoY and 14% QoQ, led by domestic sales of INR2,854 crore (+22% YoY). Exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore, with high-horsepower exports up 16% but low-horsepower exports down 20%. Profit before tax before exceptional items was INR721 crore, marginally lower YoY, as steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper inflation, freight and West Asia disruption weighed on margins. Management took one price increase at the start of Q2 FY27 and said it had not yet been absorbed by the market; no price hike was taken in Q1. Data centres drove a large share of power generation growth.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before tax before exceptional items

segments.name: Power generation (domestic)
segments.commentary: INR1,424 crore, +35% YoY. Data centres were about 40% of power gen revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 23% in Q1 FY26. Split by range: LHP INR77 crore, MHP INR248 crore, HD INR125 crore, with HHP the remainder.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR886 crore, +14% YoY and +16% QoQ, slowing from a 20%-plus five-year CAGR. Management said the slowdown reflects a higher base, parts availability and supply disruption, and reiterated 20% growth potential.

segments.name: Industrial (domestic)
segments.commentary: INR458 crore, +10% YoY. Construction INR148 crore (flat YoY), rail INR145 crore (strong order book), compressor INR52 crore, marine INR50 crore; mining, defence and others the remainder.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR521 crore, flat YoY. HHP INR296 crore (+16% YoY), LHP INR180 crore (-20% YoY). Middle East weak due to West Asia crisis; Europe and Asia Pacific were the main growth markets.

guidance_outlook: Management expects strong demand in end markets to sustain, with inflation and supply chain constraints likely to continue through the year.
Will not give a gross margin target; says margins can improve from here but cannot say whether they will return to historic highs of about 36-37%.
One price increase taken at the start of Q2 FY27; further increases will depend on market absorption and cost recovery is not expected to be full.
Employee cost of about INR2,300 crore is a higher base for the remaining quarters, per management's confirmation.
Related-party export approvals are for the current fiscal year only and are a governance measure, not a signal of an existing UK order book.
Royalty rates standardised at 4% from a previous 1% to 8% range, which explains the higher royalty ratio.
capex_capacity: Capex is in line with the last few years and goes into existing plants; utilisation is 70-75% and rising.
High-HP genset capacity is tight across the industry; demand is outpacing capacity additions, and some orders may be lost on relationships and preference, not only supply.
No plans yet to build domestic capacity for QSK78 or QSK95; India data-centre volume is still mainly QSK60, with growing interest in QSK78 and QSK95.
BESS demonstrator installed at the Phaltan rebuild centre; management says it is close to first orders but has none yet.
demand_pricing: Power gen: strong order velocity across data centres, manufacturing, residential, commercial and realty; data-centre customers asked for earlier deliveries rather than deferrals.

Pricing: commodity costs (steel, pig iron, aluminium, copper), freight and supplier labour shortages drove the cost pressure; one price hike was taken at the start of Q2 and its market acceptance is unknown.
Data-centre pricing is order-by-order; lead time and site readiness matter more to customers than price.
Rail demand is strong (power cars, diesel-electric tower cars, hotel load converters); mining tenders are recovering; construction is flat with no new national highway tenders; marine is lumpy.
Exports: Middle East orders are not coming through as expected; Europe and Asia Pacific are growing. Management would not split exports by end segment.
Competition in power gen is intense, with more than 10-12 competitors cited.

qa_highlights.question: Are capacity constraints causing lost orders in QSK60/QSK95, and have lead times lengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is outpacing supply for all high-HP players; capacity is being added at specific nodes. Management said order losses depend on customer relationships and preferences as well as supply.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margins return to the historical 36-37% from Q2 after price action?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity increases are unprecedented and it could not say whether margins would hit historic highs. It expects margins to improve as cost management gets better.

qa_highlights.question: Is the related-party export approval linked to an existing UK subsidiary order book?
qa_highlights.answer: The approval covers only the current fiscal year and is purely anticipatory; order books are built 2-3 months ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 14% distribution growth, and can it return to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown reflects a higher base and parts availability issues. It believes distribution can grow 20% over this year and the next few years, helped by penetration, retrofits and service contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre share of power gen, and what is the segment mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres were 40% of Q1 FY27 power gen revenue, up from 23% in Q1 FY26. Power gen split: LHP INR77 crore, MHP INR248 crore, HD INR125 crore; industrial split: construction INR148 crore, rail INR145 crore, compressor INR52 crore, marine INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise sharply with flat headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: the April 1, 2026 merit increase, a Q1 true-up of variable pay, and an actuarial credit booked in the prior quarter that lowered last quarter's cost.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on whether the Q2 price increase is absorbed and on commodity and freight trends; management gave no margin target.
Export weakness from the Middle East (West Asia crisis) and LHP export decline of 20% YoY.
Distribution growth slowed to 14% in Q1; watch whether it returns toward the 20% level management cites.
High-HP capacity constraints and rising data-centre concentration (40% of power gen revenue) could limit growth or raise concentration risk.
Management succession: the MD said the parent is looking for a successor.
Higher related-party dealings with CTIL and the parent; management says the approvals are only for the current year and that scale drives the choice of entity.
500480|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the data-centre pipeline, but cautious and at times evasive on margins, pricing outcomes, exports and the medium-term outlook, citing unprecedented commodity and geopolitical conditions. Management declined to share price-hike size, market share, segment margins and capacity plans beyond current nodes.
key_quotes: Demand is outpacing supply for everyone.
I will not be able to say whether we will hit historic highs or not, because these are unprecedented times in terms of commodity increases and inflation coming at the same time.
This is purely in anticipation, Jonas, just as a prudent governance practice and order books don't get built this early in the year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity is being added at specific existing nodes and high-HP demand outpaces supply for all players, but management gave no new plant or line date and declined to share capacity plans beyond current nodes; utilisation is 70-75% and rising.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic sales rose 22% YoY to INR2,854 crore, power gen +35% YoY to INR1,424 crore with data centres at 40% of power gen revenue, and order velocity is strong; exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore with LHP down 20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held in line with the last few years and goes into existing plants; utilisation is 70-75%, below the 80%+ level that would normally force a new capex announcement, and there are no plans for domestic QSK78/QSK95 capacity.

rows.why: No numeric guidance was given; management was cautious on margins, exports and the medium-term outlook, and Middle East orders are not coming through as expected.

rows.why: BESS demonstrator is installed at the Phaltan rebuild centre and management says it is close to first orders, but it has none yet; no other product launch was discussed.

rows.label: Q2 FY27 price increase absorption
rows.why: One price increase was taken at the start of Q2 FY27 after no hike in Q1, and management said the market has not yet absorbed it, so acceptance and cost recovery are uncertain.

rows.label: Europe and Asia Pacific export growth vs Middle East weakness
rows.why: Exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore, with high-HP exports up 16% YoY to INR296 crore while Middle East orders are not coming through and LHP exports fell 20% YoY to INR180 crore.

rows.label: Rail order book strength
rows.why: Rail sales were INR145 crore in Q1 FY27 with a strong order book (power cars, diesel-electric tower cars, hotel load converters), supporting industrial growth from INR458 crore (+10% YoY).

tone.note: Management was confident on data-centre demand, order velocity and high-HP capacity tightness, but cautious and at times evasive on gross margin recovery, price-hike outcomes, exports and the medium-term outlook; analysts pushed on margins, distribution slowdown to 14% and related-party exports.

500493|2026-03.headline: Bharat Forge FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% to INR 16,812 crore, but standalone revenue fell 5% to INR 8,396 crore on US and CV demand headwinds.
500493|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR 16,812 crore (up 11%) and EBITDA INR 2,921 crore (up about 6%), with consolidated net debt-to-equity at 0.41x. Standalone revenue fell about 5% YoY to INR 8,396 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR 2,312 crore (27.5% margin), though Q4 standalone revenue rose 8.5% QoQ to INR 2,260 crore on export recovery and domestic auto strength. Management is restructuring the German steel subsidiary (CDP Bharat Forge) over roughly 15-18 months, is taking an e-mobility investment write-off, and is pushing growth in aerospace, defence and JSA castings. Management guided to about 25% growth for India operations in FY27, barring geopolitical shocks.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone PBT before exceptional items FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 610 crore (27% margin; about 28% excluding INR 11 crore one-time MSEDCL charge)

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone PBT before exceptional items Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 3,865 crore revenue; INR 151 crore EBITDA (4% margin)
INR 1,534 crore revenue; INR 54 crore EBITDA (3.5% margin)
INR 4,814 crore (traditional INR 1,210 crore; defence INR 2,816 crore; JSA INR 292 crore; K-Drive about INR 500 crore)

segments.name: Standalone (auto + industrial components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 8,396 crore (-5% YoY) hit by North American regulatory uncertainty and US CV demand; Q4 recovered 8.5% QoQ on exports and domestic auto. Tariff cost absorbed in Q4 was about INR 12 crore.

segments.name: Defence (KSSL)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,562 crore; order book close to INR 11,000 crore with stable revenue accretion expected over 3-4 years. Management expects 30-40% growth guidance from earlier call to be carried by ATAGS and CQB carbine milestones.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 400 crore; now about 26% of Q4 industrial non-auto exports and the second-largest industrial export contributor. Margins stated as above company average; target INR 1,000 crore in about 3 years.

segments.name: JSA (castings)
segments.commentary: Secured INR 292 crore of new business in FY26; growth continuing despite weak wind export demand. Raised external capital from Premji Invest to fund capacity expansion as an independent business.

segments.name: K-Drive (axles)
segments.commentary: Acquired recently; secured about INR 500 crore of new business. Management sees revenue doubling in 3-4 years, with a goal of mid-teens margins.

segments.name: Europe and US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Europe EBITDA margin 4% and US 3.5% in FY26. German CDP steel business is being wound up via solvent liquidation, to complete around end CY27, with losses expected to fall.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India operations (standalone plus Indian subsidiaries) expected to grow close to 25%, barring further geopolitical disruption; growth to come mainly from aerospace, defence and automotive components, with aerospace growing faster than defence.
Overseas losses expected to reduce as CDP losses fall away during restructuring, with completion around end of CY27.
Capex of INR 800-850 crore over a 15-18 month period across forging, casting and products platforms.
Defence revenue to see ATAGS and CQB carbine production start in H2 FY27; large project backlog to start in H2 of this year.
Explosives facility in Andhra Pradesh: groundbreaking this month, construction by end of year, ready in under 15 months, pilot production 6-8 months later (about 24 months overall).
Data-centre orders to start contributing from Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp up in FY28.
capex_capacity: Ongoing capex programmes across forging, casting and products platforms to total INR 800-850 crore over 15-18 months; management gave no FY28+ figure beyond this.
ATAGS initial production capacity about five guns per month; testing expected to complete in H2 FY27 before production and supplies start.
Explosives plant planned in Andhra Pradesh, subject to significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending, expected in 2-4 months.

Acquired 30% stake in Fortuna Engineering (Nashik) for INR 130 crore; company has revenue about INR 380 crore and net cash about INR 20 crore, and plans to add new machining lines (mid-teens EBITDA/EBIT margin).
JSA capacity expansion funded by Premji Invest capital raise; plan to shift some manufacturing from Europe to India.
demand_pricing: US CV: management says outlook strong, citing aging fleet replacement and emission norms due early 2027; energy price rise a common industry issue.
India CV: demand expected to be reasonably stable as energy costs are passed along the value chain.
US passenger car market stable at about 16-16.1 million vehicles, similar to last year; Europe seen as more challenged due to prolonged war.
Energy cost is the biggest cost issue; management is negotiating compensation with customers for energy-intensive elements.
Aerospace: multiple new wins across jet engine structures and landing systems; selected as first Indian supplier of critical components by a global aerospace OEM.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be broken down by defence, US CV, non-auto and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined granular split; said higher growth from aerospace, then defence, then components (auto and industrial). Outlook strong for both US and India CV.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% India growth is standalone versus Indian subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it; the 25% target is at overall India level, covering standalone plus Indian subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: Will German CDP losses disappear from operating numbers now that restructuring has started?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses go away as the entity is wound up, expected by end of CY27; restructuring is a 15-18 month process combining customer transition and solvent liquidation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the defence revenue timing and milestones from the INR 2,816 crore of new defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: ATAGS and CQB carbine production to start H2 FY27; data-centre-related orders begin Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp in FY28; large backlog projects in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY28 explosives capex been confirmed as the heavy spend year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the explosives plant in Andhra Pradesh is about 24 months from groundbreaking to pilot production, with construction starting by end-2026 after approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise external capital in JSA when it could be funded internally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise lets JSA grow with its own momentum, as it could become a multi-thousand-crore business, with plans to shift European casting manufacturing to India.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and energy price spikes affecting costs, transport and demand; management says it is too early to say the worst is past.
Overseas losses (Europe EBITDA margin 4%, US 3.5%) must narrow as CDP is wound down, with completion around end CY27.
Defence revenue ramp depends on ATAGS testing completion and production start in H2 FY27; the order-book conversion timing remains open.
Explosives plant needs significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending.
Management declined to disclose defence share of revenue, K-Drive/Fortuna-level detail, or a timeline for a possible defence listing ("will look at separately").

key_quotes: Barring any further geopolitical crisis and their impact on demand, we should see a close to 25% growth in our India business.

500493|2026-09.headline: Bharat Forge Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 30% YoY to INR2,526 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.9%.

Consolidated revenue was INR4,870 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR778 crore (up about 9%, around 16% margin). Freight, energy and input cost inflation compressed margins, with pass-through to customers lagging; management flagged an optical impact of about 0.4% on margins. Defence order book stood at INR10,950 crore as of September, and the ATAGS bulk production clearance has been received, with revenue recognition expected from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: India manufacturing margin expected to add 200-250 bps; K-Drive targets double-digit EBITDA margin within 2 years with 20-25% annual growth, expanding into passenger car, SUV, pickup and utility segments.

qa_highlights.answer: Steel subsidiary had one-time breakdowns, with a fix targeted by December; aluminium subsidiary has raw material cost issues and new non-auto products expected to lift profitability in 6-12 months.

500495|2026-03.headline: Escorts Kubota Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to INR386.0 crore (13.1% margin); FY27 tractor industry guided flat to ±3%.
500495|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone operating revenue from continuing operations rose 21.4% YoY to INR2,950.7 crore, with PAT from continuing operations up 29.6% to INR324.8 crore (about 20% excluding a prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment). FY26 was a record year: tractor volume 1,33,670 units (+15.7%), revenue INR11,472.8 crore (+12.6%) and EBITDA INR1,513 crore (13.2% margin). Management guided FY27 industry flat to +/-3%, with H1 flat and H2 a substantial decline on a high base, low monsoon and El Nino risk, and rising input costs. Management expects input-cost pressure to be significant over the next two quarters, with only about 1.5% price increase taken in April.

financial_highlights.change: +29.6% YoY; ~20% YoY excluding prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment

segments.name: Agri Machinery (tractors, implements, engines, services)
segments.commentary: FY26 segment revenue INR9,709.6 crore (+15.8%). Domestic tractor volume 1,26,994 units (+14.9%); exports 6,676 tractors (+33.8%). Non-tractor share of segment revenue fell to 18% from 20%.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR556.5 crore (+22.6%), EBITDA margin 12.7% (+386 bps). FY26 volume 5,794 units (-10.6%); Q4 volume about 1,877 units (+9%) versus served industry about +4%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic tractor industry guided flat to +2-3% or -2-3%; H1 FY27 at par, H2 a substantial decline on high base, sub-normal monsoon forecast and El Nino (about 65-70% probability).
Management expects market share and volume growth in FY27 irrespective of industry outcome, citing new products and channel fixes.
Input costs: management estimates a 5-6% cost increase; steel up 7-8%, tyres asked 15-20%, base metals double-digit. Significant pressure expected in the next two quarters.

Management aims to maintain full-year EBIT margin, but said this is too early to call; permanent labour and energy cost increases (Haryana contract wages up about 35%, UP vendor costs up 22-23%) will not reverse.
FY27 capex: normal capex INR350-400 crore; greenfield about INR500 crore in FY27; captive finance capital infusion about INR300 crore by year-end and INR200 crore next year.
Long-term tractor industry CAGR assumed 6-8%; FY28 seen as reasonably good given emission norm change from 1 April 2028.
capex_capacity: Normal capex about INR311 crore in FY26 (cash flow); FY27 normal capex guided at INR350-400 crore, of which majority is product development (about INR200 crore in FY26, INR200-250 crore planned FY27).

Greenfield plant: land initial payment made, balance payment expected within the quarter; Phase 1 more than INR2,000 crore; over 7-10 years total spend above INR5,000 crore covering tractors, construction equipment and possibly Agri Solutions.
Captive finance company: Board approval INR700 crore of capital, INR200 crore invested so far, portfolio above INR100 crore at end-March; balance INR500 crore over 12-15 months.
Construction equipment capacity utilisation was about 47% last year per analyst; mini excavators to be manufactured in India only after new plant is ready (currently imported from Japan).
demand_pricing: Regional FY26 tractor growth: North and Central about 16-17% versus about 30% in West and South, which management attributed largely to subsidies. FY27 headwind expected mainly in West and South; North flat to nil growth.
Product gaps: paddy special tractors for southern markets launched, with early signs of share loss in South stabilising; further launches planned over next 3-4 months across three brands.
Price increase of about 1.5% taken in April across tractors and construction equipment; management says this is not sufficient to offset cost inflation.
Around 70% of tractor sales are financed; captive finance launched to speed approvals.

Construction equipment: served industry down about 7% in FY26 (crane -13%, backloader -10%, mini excavator +38%, compactor +5%); Q4 served industry +4%. Crane market share gained 2.7%; number 1 in mini excavators.
Exports: Kubota Global channel about 60% of tractor exports; crane exports rising to 5-6% of revenue from about 3-3.5%, target 10% by 2030. Agri Solutions harvesting and planting portfolio expanding.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company planning FY27 tractor industry growth and new product contribution to share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra guided FY27 industry flat to +/-2-3% and said volume and share growth look positive irrespective of industry, citing paddy special tractors and further launches over the next 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q4 margin softness and what is the cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan attributed the QoQ dip mainly to mix (new products and higher non-tractor revenue, which carry lower margins) and noted commodity inflation mostly lands in the next two quarters; full-year margin maintenance is the aim, subject to geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of commodity impact and price hikes needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a 5-6% cost increase versus revenue (base metals double-digit inflation); April price hike of about 1.5% was insufficient; some one-off costs may be amortised over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for construction equipment and the export opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Bajaj expects a turnaround after monsoon if macro issues settle within 1-1.5 quarters; cranes exports rising; mini excavators are fully imported from Japan until India manufacturing starts.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance (about INR7,000 crore including investments) be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan said greenfield Phase 1 is above INR2,000 crore within a more than INR5,000 crore 7-10 year plan, plus the captive finance infusion, and some surplus will remain on the balance sheet for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Captive finance capital and ROE aspirations?
qa_highlights.answer: Up to INR700 crore capital approved (INR200 crore invested); long-term ROE for captive finance companies seen at about 1.5-2%, with the primary aim being to support tractor sales.

H2 FY27 tractor demand decline from high base, sub-normal monsoon, El Nino and reservoir levels below last year and 10-year average.
West Asia conflict, shipping disruption and rupee depreciation affecting costs and supply chain.

500495|2026-06.headline: Escorts Kubota Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR3,178.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.2% from 13.1% on commodity inflation.
500495|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from continuing operations grew 28% YoY to INR3,178.9 crore, with tractor domestic volume at a record 35,457 units (+22.9%) and market share up 36 bps. Standalone EBITDA rose 9.4% to INR355.4 crore, but margin compressed 190 bps to 11.2% as metal and rubber commodity inflation (about 5% on tractors per management) hit costs. Net profit growth of 4% reported is distorted by a INR76 crore land-sale gain and RED divestment in the base quarter; management cites 26% growth excluding the gain. Management raised its FY27 industry outlook to mid-to-mid-single-digit growth from a prior plus/minus 2-3% view, and flagged a further 1.5-2% cost pressure in Q2 with price hikes under discussion.

segments.name: Tractor exports
segments.commentary: Exports fell to 1,405 units from 1,733 (down about 19%) while industry exports rose 17.7% to 29,778; vessel availability and weak sub-40 HP compact exports (down ~8%) hurt. Kubota global network accounts for ~61% of export volume.

segments.name: Agri Machinery non-tractor business
segments.commentary: Agri Solutions, engines and spares/service parts were 19% of Agri Machinery revenue vs 18% a year earlier. Component exports were flat in Q1 and about INR160-170 crore last year.

Construction equipment industry FY27 growth 12-15%: mini excavators and cranes high, backhoe loaders 5-7%, compactors 5-6%. Escorts CE expected to grow 12-15% for the full year.

Captive finance penetration 10-12% of dealers in Q1, nearing 15% in July; 40-50% of dealerships targeted by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra said there is upside in Q1 and July; the earlier guidance was plus/minus 2-3%, not negative, and the last 45-50 days were very positive. Current view is middle to mid-single-digit industry growth for FY27, with no quarterly or monthly estimate given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q1 metal cost headwind, and how will Q2 margins and pricing be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan said the tractor business absorbed about 5% commodity cost impact, of which about 1% was Haryana contract-labour wages. Q2 faces a further 1.5-2%; a price hike of about 1-1.5% was taken in April, and the next hike is under discussion with timing expected in Q2. Relief is expected from Q4 if geopolitics ease.
