Powertrac has a gap in 35-50 HP 4WD, to be covered in the next few months. Kubota focus is 20-30 HP and 41-50 HP segments, which make up roughly 70-80% of the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes and growth expectations apply to construction equipment cranes, and is there customer pushback?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Bajaj said cumulative price increases are about 6% after channel discount adjustments, passed on in small tranches since January 2025. Crane industry grew about 45% in Q1 on a subdued base. Customers are negotiating longer, and prices are expected to stabilise in Q2. CE industry FY27 growth guided at 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the southern market share trending, and how is captive finance performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra said South share is about 6% on a 3-brand basis, gained about 0.5-0.6 pp in Q1, and new products and channel fill are expected to continue the trend. Bharat Madan said captive finance penetration was 10-12% of dealers in Q1, near 15% in July, across about 250 onboarded dealers; 40-50% of dealerships by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the component export trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan guided FY27 tractor exports roughly flat, with the Q1 shortfall expected to be recovered over three quarters, and FY28 growth including a possible North America entry. Component exports were flat in Q1 against about INR160-170 crore last year, with growth expected from H2 and more than doubling over two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and could FY28 capex rise? Is a buyback possible?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR850-900 crore: INR450-500 crore greenfield land (already paid, groundbreaking expected in August) and INR350-400 crore normal capex. Total greenfield outlay is about INR2,000 crore, and FY28 spend could rise if construction is accelerated. On buyback, Bharat Madan said promoters hold about 68%+, so scope is limited and promoter alignment is needed.

500495|2026-09.headline: Escorts Kubota Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.0% from 13.1% YoY on commodity inflation, despite revenue up 16.3% to INR3,231.4 crores.

Net profit fell to INR255 crores from INR321.2 crores. Domestic tractor volumes were flat-to-up at 32,628 units while the industry declined about 3%, and construction equipment grew strongly. Management guided to continued margin pressure in Q3, with recovery expected from Q4 as a new price increase of about 3-3.5% takes effect from mid-November.

segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR2,690.1 crores (+10.6%); non-tractor (Agri Solutions, engines, spares and service) now 22% of segment revenue vs 17% a year ago. EBIT margin 7.8%.

Commodity inflation about 5% in Q1 rising to 8-9% by end-Q2; about 75-80% from commodities and 20% from manpower and conversion costs. Further 2-3% inflation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much industry decline is expected in H2 and what is the regional split?

qa_highlights.question: Will the non-tractor business margins be comparable to tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-tractor business is broadly comparable to tractor margins overall, with imported harvester trading lower and parts and locally made engines at good margins; non-tractor is 18% of revenue, tractors about 65%, CE about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 22% YoY and 14% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher production to build inventory for the season (production above sales by 20-25%) increased overhead absorption; there was a one-time inventory benefit of about 1.5% that reverses in Q3; contractual manpower costs in Haryana rose 35% from April.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and greenfield plans?

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable CE margin?

500520|2026-09.headline: M&M Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 25% to ₹4,588 crore on revenue of ₹57,553 crore, with full-year tractor industry outlook cut to flattish.
500520|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 25% to ₹57,553 crore and PAT rose 25% to ₹4,588 crore, with year-to-date profit up 29% and ROE at 21%. Growth came from multiple businesses (Logistics turnaround, Accelo, Mahindra Finance, Tech M, Growth Gems) while Farm fell 9% on a festive-season shift and weak international subsidiaries. Management cut its full-year tractor industry outlook from +5% to flattish, citing a weaker monsoon (87% of LPA vs 90% earlier) and drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Auto demand remains supply-constrained, with waiting periods of 5–7 months on Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, and capacity is set to rise from 66,000 to 82,000 units/month this year and 92,000 next year.

segments.name: Auto (SUV, LCV, EV)
segments.commentary: PAT up 55% with SUV and LCV volumes strong; ICE capacity 61k and EV 8k reached 73k+ units in October, with EV penetration at 12–12.7% of SUVs. Prices raised 5% in Auto to offset commodity inflation.

segments.name: Farm (tractors)
segments.commentary: Profit down 9% on festive-season shift, weak monsoon and international drag; Farm prices raised 4%. Full-year industry tractor outlook cut to flattish from +5%; the three global subsidiaries face US -15%, Brazil -18%, Turkey -36%.

segments.name: Mahindra Finance
segments.commentary: PAT up 61% (after 55% last quarter) on lower asset quality and tech/data gains; AUM above ₹1,30,000 crore against ₹65,000 crore starting point.

segments.name: Tech Mahindra
segments.commentary: PAT up 33%, with large deal wins and a strong pipeline; AI adoption accelerating.

segments.name: Logistics and Growth Gems
segments.commentary: Logistics turned from loss-making last year to a good profit level; Growth Gems profit up 3X again, Accelo up 70%.

segments.name: Last Mile Mobility (Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, Suman Mishra)
segments.commentary: Capacity capped; ~45,000 units in quarter, all electric. Industry 3W electrification at 45–50%, with L5M estimated at 70%+; capacity up 25% over last 1.5 years and further expansion planned.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahindra Aerostructures)
segments.commentary: Order book growing; new Airbus A320neo skin/fuselage tail package won, plus single-source helicopter fuselage supply. Management targets $1bn annual orders by FY30 and says it is at 28X the base.

segments.name: Lifespaces
segments.commentary: Pre-sales reached 5X of the decade target (14X). Bhandup project spans 35–37 acres; capital deployed only once profitability was confirmed.

demand_pricing: Auto demand is strong across brands; waiting periods are 5–7 months for Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, and about 1.5–2 months for most other products.

Shift in powertrain mix: away from petrol toward CNG, EV and, surprisingly, diesel; the company says the festive season saw no slowdown in SUVs, including in rural areas, except in parts of the South.
EV cumulative sales above 1 lakh; 9S is the highest-selling EV; BE 6 launched 15 August.
Auto prices raised by 5%, Farm by 4%; management says pricing has not hurt demand.
Management stopped sharing order book data because of cancellation noise.

qa_highlights.question: How has demand shaped up after the GST cut, and what changed in powertrain mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand stayed robust with no SUV slowdown in rural areas; petrol has lost share to CNG, EV and diesel. Vahan like-for-like festive volumes were roughly flat to minus, and M&M is the fastest-growing brand on Vahan.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&M planning capacity for full utilisation given structural shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity went from 17,000 five years ago to 66,000 now and will be 82,000 at year end and 92,000 next year; a Nagpur plant and a supplier park will double capacity with room to expand quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for EV demand after fuel prices fall, and localisation of batteries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says EV adoption has passed a tunnelling inflection; pump prices are unlikely to fall soon. Battery packs are already localised; cells will be sourced overseas unless captive supply is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor outlook for next year given monsoon normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NOAA's normal monsoon probability above 70% next year and a flat industry even in a strong El Niño year; the Navratri shift will support Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much PLI was booked and what is the EV margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹1,000 crore PLI booked this quarter. EV margins are around 9% helped by PLI; management expects volume, supplier leverage and pricing power to take margins toward ICE levels over time, with depreciation the main drag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international Farm subsidiaries after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Sampo and Erkunt exits are complete; Mitsubishi Mahindra Agricultural Machinery Japan closes by Q4. Exit costs from 3Q and 4Q last year will not recur, helping Farm consolidation in H2.

500530|2026-03.headline: Bosch Ltd to acquire related-party Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) for INR9,068.7 crore, ~10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA, targeted close by end-Q1 FY27.
500530|2026-03.overview: This transcript covers two investor calls on April 13, 2026, about the proposed acquisition of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt Ltd (RBIC), a group company, not a quarterly results call; management said it was in silent period and would not discuss quarterly results. RBIC posted FY25 revenue of about INR4,000 crore and a 19.3% EBITDA margin, with 9M FY26 revenue of about INR3,500 crore. Pro forma FY25 revenue for Bosch Ltd rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore and EBITDA margin improves from 12.8% to 13.9%, with about 5% pro forma EPS accretion. The deal is almost all cash, funded from existing funds and internal accruals, with a small preferential allotment to Robert Bosch Netherlands and Robert Bosch US, and shareholder voting runs April 9 to May 8, 2026.

Pro forma FY25 EBITDA margin (Bosch Ltd)

segments.commentary: Covers ABS, ESP, occupant safety sensors and controllers, EV new braking systems (iBooster, integrated power brakes) and conventional actuation; about one-third two-wheeler and the rest passenger and commercial vehicles per management's rough estimate. Three plants (Chakan, Manesar, Sanand) and about 2,000 people including contract workers.

segments.name: Bosch Ltd - power solutions and aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retains powertrain/propulsion and mobility aftermarket. Management said the portfolios are complementary with no overlap. Bosch Automotive Electronics (captive contract manufacturer, low margin, high capex) is excluded from this deal and is under review.

Dividend distribution policy of 55%-85% of PAT reiterated.
capex_capacity: Target's main plant is in Chakan; a large plant in Jharkhand; Manesar is an assembly unit and Sanand a warehouse, with management saying the current capacity is near max in its current locations.
Expansion is mostly brownfield, using idle lines from the Bosch global network (second-hand, pre-run lines) for faster ramp-up.
Each e-axle line produces about 150,000 units; the e-axle market is small in India and the 50:50 JV with Tata Autocomp is intended to consolidate volumes.
Management says it will add capacity only against legislation or confirmed OEM programmes.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is very full, with a project pipeline for 4-5 years, and that no orders have been lost so far.
Two-wheeler ABS: management says Bosch holds a very high, market-leading share; a below-125cc ABS mandate is still under consideration with no new update.
Margins expected to face some pressure from OEMs wanting customized solutions and from cost-down pressure in ABS for the 2-wheeler segment, but management expects to hold margins steady.
Management said it is the market leader in passenger car ABS/ESP and the most advanced ESP is 10th generation.
Localization is over 90% of child parts for some Bosch Ltd products, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was RBIC chosen now, and why not Bosch Automotive Electronics (related-party exposure)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBIC is powertrain-agnostic and margin-accretive from day one. The automotive electronics entity is a captive, low-margin, capex-heavy contract manufacturer and is excluded for now but under ongoing review.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix and synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly one-third two-wheeler and the rest cars and commercial vehicles. No synergies counted in the business case; they will be reviewed in post-merger integration.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the margin jump (gross margin from ~34% to ~40%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, localization of products and child parts, legislation-led volume, modular platforms, and idle lines transferred from the Bosch network, with stable quality and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a preferential issue of only about INR8.8 crore disclosed and not the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The company secretary said the announcement covered only the preferential issue and that the acquisition details were UPSI before the board meeting. The questioner challenged the disclosure, and management said it would improve governance practice.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, funding and balance sheet after deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash consideration is covered and both companies will be debt-free post-deal. The company did not disclose the target's H1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Order book at RBIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the order book as very full, with a 4-5 year project pipeline and good market share in all categories.

Shareholder approval through the voting window ending May 8, 2026, and completion targeted by end-Q1 FY27.
Management views on the 2-wheeler ABS mandate for sub-125cc bikes remain unconfirmed; the deal business case excludes unlegislated upside.
Margin pressure in ABS for 2-wheelers and from Chinese competitors; the transfer price and cost-based structure will need monitoring post-close.
RBIC cash flow and capex figures were not disclosed; the cash flow figures stated as of 9M FY26 are unconfirmed.

500530|2026-06.headline: Bosch Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR58,419 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR8,180 million, with EBITDA margin near 14%.
500530|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR58,419 million, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, led by Power Solutions and 2-wheeler Powersports. EBITDA was INR8,180 million (up 28% YoY, 4.7% QoQ), and management attributed the margin gain to revenue growth and expense optimisation. Reported PAT of INR7,018 million fell 37.1% YoY because the prior year included an exceptional gain on sale of video solutions and access/intrusion businesses; excluding it, PAT grew 9.9%. Management said the Chassis Systems acquisition was completed in July and consolidation starts this quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew 9.6% YoY and 8.7% QoQ, driven by lubricants, batteries, spark plugs and braking systems; independent aftermarket recorded its highest-ever monthly sales in June.

segments.name: 2-wheeler and Powersports
segments.commentary: Grew 41.4% YoY on value-added EMS products and premium motorcycle platforms; management said it gained market share and reported zero production disruptions.

segments.commentary: Grew 20.9% YoY on tool demand and marketing campaigns, but declined 15.7% QoQ on seasonal factors.

CAFE Phase 3 norms from April 2027 are expected to boost Power Solutions further; CV ADAS regulation starts October 2027.

500530|2026-09.headline: Bosch Ltd Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.6% to INR61,641 mn and EBITDA 30.1% to INR8,028 mn, with H2 guided modest.

Standalone EBITDA margin was about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in the prior two quarters, as aluminium prices and a weaker rupee against the euro offset volume absorption. A one-time reversal of long-term service award provision (INR1,240 mn standalone, INR1,304 mn consolidated) sits in exceptional items and lifted reported PAT. Management guided to a more modest H2 on inflation, weak monsoon, tighter rates and a high base, and announced a 3:1 bonus issue and a split of INR10 shares into INR2 face value, subject to shareholder approval.

500550|2026-03.headline: Siemens Ltd Q4 FY26 (March quarter): orders up 33% to ₹67.3bn and revenue up 14.6% to ₹46.2bn, but EBITDA margin fell 290bp to 9.7% on commodity and FX costs.
500550|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong order intake and revenue growth in the March 2026 quarter, with all three businesses growing revenue double digits. Profitability was hit by material costs rising to 74% of revenue from 69% in Q2, driven by a roughly 18% Euro depreciation against INR and sharp rises in silver and copper. Backlog reached ₹450bn, up 9.3%, including a ₹18bn export bogie order executable over 2029-2039. Management gave no quarterly margin guidance and said two price increases have been taken in DI and SI, with a 3-4 month lag before they flow through.

segments.name: Smart Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹29.6bn (+17.6%, book-to-bill 1.15); revenue ₹25.8bn (+14.5%). 6M orders ₹60.6bn (+22.9%), revenue +11.6%, EBITDA margin 15.1% vs 16.2% (down 120bp) on commodity costs. Volumes grew 17.5% in Q4 and 23% in 6M.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that government ordering softens given fiscal pressure?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nashik factories be expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is examining expansion for both factories given the backlog and pipeline and will update later. Metro rolling stock capacity decisions remain open.

capex_capacity: India FY26 capex about Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of revenue), within guided range for combined PV and EV capex.
Sierra supply constrained by casting suppliers on the new engine; immediate milestone is to cross 10,000 units a month with additional suppliers added.
EV run rate about 24,000 a quarter on average and about 27,000 in Q4, with a monthly run rate of about 9,000; production to rise by about 10% from May.
JLR investment is largely in UK plant facilities for three new architectures and BEV powertrains at the Wolverhampton propulsion facility.
Dealer inventory in India about 20 days; waiting periods 4-8 weeks, longer for Sierra and certain EVs.
demand_pricing: India industry FY26 volumes hit a record 4.7 million units (+8%); H2 grew 17% post GST 2.0, and April-May demand momentum stayed at a high level.
Nexon and Punch ranked number one and number three models in the industry during H2 FY26.
EV bookings up roughly 25-30% after the Middle East crisis began in February, though supply, not demand, is the constraint.

JLR ASPs fell marginally QoQ to about GBP 72,000 from GBP 76,000, mainly due to sterling strength against the dollar ($1.36 Q4 average vs $1.325 in Q3). Q4 gross margin fell on higher VME (7% vs 5% last year) and warranty charges.
JLR China volumes fell 27% YoY in FY26 due to luxury tax and dealer-stock reduction; US retailer stock brought down after tariffs, now slightly below normal levels.
Middle East (6% of JLR sales mix) expected to be hit in Q1 FY27; Middle East dealers are running out of stock.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the commodity headwind, and how will it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated the impact at 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months, with about 2% offset by cost reductions in FY26 and 0.5% price increase taken in April. Further measured price increases are under consideration but not decided.

qa_highlights.question: Will EV volumes step up, and will net pricing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: EV run rate is about 9,000 a month and expected to rise above 10,000 from May; demand is strong but supply constrained. Long-term EV cost trends are deflationary versus inflationary ICE costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Range Rover EV launch timing and pre-bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Range Rover Electric is coming soon as the first JLR EV launch, with three reveals in H2 CY26. There are no firm pre-bookings, but about 78,000 expressions of interest.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitics and fuel prices affecting EV demand and investment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Middle East war does not change launch timelines or investment plans, but JLR will need to keep ICE, PHEV, MHEV and BEV offerings in parallel for longer than planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is JLR planning to reduce its breakeven volume to 300,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP 1.7 billion plan covers end-to-end procurement (now a separate Board-level vertical), warranty cost reduction and IT/digital productivity; benefits to start from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 industry growth and TMPV's supply situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth expected at about 10%, with high double-digit H1. Management said FY27 is a supply challenge rather than demand, with two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV planned.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a prior-period item in Q4 PLI accrual?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about Rs 90 Cr related to Q3 that was certified in Q4; excluding it, Q4 PLI would be about Rs 380 Cr against Rs 471 Cr reported.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, petrochemical-linked inputs) of 5-6% of revenue with limited pass-through so far; margin depends on further price actions and cost savings.
Middle East conflict: Q1 FY27 demand hit in JLR's 6% Middle East mix and potential component or freight disruption, though no shortages seen yet.
Sierra and EV supply ramp is dependent on casting suppliers and new capacity; EV volumes are constrained despite strong demand.
JLR warranty cost increases (notably the US) and rising VME (7% vs 5%) continue to pressure margins.
Sterling strength against the dollar and tariffs weigh on JLR cash flow; FY26 cash flow was impacted by lower payables.
China luxury tax and the Chinese OEM push in Europe and the UK pose competitive risks for JLR.
key_quotes: So as expected, we did recover strongly in Q4.
Having said that, and delivered what we promised in Q4, it is accepted that our full year financial performance is far from what we had intended when we started the year.
The issue is supply. It will completely depend on ramping up, how fast we are able to ramp up the volumes.
So, given this new world order in supply and demand side of our business, what's our response?
Demand for the moment is slightly a secondary concern.
500570|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on India demand and the H2 rebound, with management stating demand is strong and the constraint is supply. Cautious and candid on JLR, admitting full-year performance was far from intended and calling for corrective action, and deferring FY27 guidance to the June investor days.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India Q4 EBITDA margin 9.4% and EBIT 4.7%, but a 5-6% of revenue commodity headwind over 9-12 months is only partly offset (about 2% cost reductions in FY26 plus a 0.5% April price hike), and JLR cost savings of GBP 1.7 bn start only from H2 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: EV production is already rising beyond 10,000 a month from May 2026 (about 10% increase), Sierra.ev launches next quarter, and management plans two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV in FY27; however, no specific new plant or capacity number was given, so this is partly backed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects FY27 industry growth of about 10% (high double digits in H1) and aims for industry-beating TMPV growth from a FY26 base of 6.42 lakh units (+15%) with Q4 above 2 lakh units; supply, not demand, is the constraint, and dealer inventory is about 20 days.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India FY26 capex was about Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of revenue) and the call did not discuss utilisation or a new plant; JLR investment is in already committed UK architecture and BEV programmes.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 JLR guidance is deferred to the 17 June 2026 Investor Day, and the call flagged a Middle East hit in Q1 FY27 plus a commodity headwind, so there is no basis for a raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: JLR FY26 EBIT came in at 0.7% against 0–2% guidance, Middle East (6% of JLR mix) demand is expected to be hit in Q1 FY27, and commodity headwinds of 5-6% of revenue are still to flow through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: next quarter (Q1 FY27) for Sierra.ev; Range Rover Electric r
rows.why: Sierra.ev launch is expected next quarter, Range Rover Electric has about 78,000 expressions of interest with three reveals in H2 CY26, and FY27 includes two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV.

rows.label: Exports growth 70-100% in FY27
rows.why: Exports were 10,000+ in FY26 and management is targeting 70% to 100% growth in FY27.

rows.label: JLR GBP 1.7 bn cost savings to cut breakeven toward 300,000 units
rows.why: Management targets GBP 1.7 bn of savings over two years, from a FY26 JLR wholesale base of 308,000 units, with benefits starting H2 FY27.

rows.label: Further measured price increases under consideration
rows.why: A 0.5% price rise was taken in April 2026 against a 5-6% of revenue commodity headwind over 9-12 months, with further increases under consideration but not decided.

tone.note: Management was confident on India demand and supply-constrained EV growth, and candid that JLR's FY26 performance (0.7% EBIT vs 0-2% guidance) was far from intended; analysts pushed on commodity pass-through, JLR breakeven and the Middle East hit.
